translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziming, Feng Xingming, Zhang Yuanhan, Yu Hongqing, Jiang Rong, Tang Yuan, and Wei Xing

translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhaoben, Pan Zhoudai, Zhang Huai, Zhang Tingbiao, Hu Qi'ai, Fang Qiming, and Deng Chengzhu

translations.idiomatic: Zhang San'ai, Yang Mengyi, Yan Tianlun, Xia Shiyou, Bai Changjiu, Guo Wei'er, and Nie Hong

sentences.zh: 董阿虎張乞人席慕孔張長松崔長生榮孝子

translations.literal: Dong Ahu, Zhang Qiren, Xi Mukong, Zhang Changsong, Cui Changsheng, and Rong Xiaozi
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ahu, Zhang Qiren, Xi Mukong, Zhang Changsong, Cui Changsheng, and Rong Xiaozi

sentences.zh: 無錫二孝子啞孝子清興關外，俗純樸，愛親敬長，內愨而外嚴。

translations.literal: In Wuxi were two filial sons and a mute filial son; when the Qing arose beyond the Pass, customs were pure and simple, loving parents and respecting elders, reserved within and stern without.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi had its pair of filial sons and its mute filial son; beyond the Pass, when the Qing dynasty arose, the people were plain and unadorned in custom, devoted to parents and respectful to elders, inwardly reserved and outwardly severe.

sentences.zh: 既定鼎，禮教益備。

translations.literal: Once the dynasty was firmly established, ritual instruction grew ever more complete.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding of the dynasty was settled, ritual teaching became ever more fully provided.

sentences.zh: 定旌格，循明舊。

translations.literal: Standards for conferring commendation were fixed, following Ming precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The criteria for imperial commendation were set, in accord with Ming practice.

sentences.zh: 親存，奉侍竭其力；

translations.literal: While parents lived, one served them with the full exertion of one's strength;
translations.idiomatic: While parents were alive, one attended them with every ounce of one's strength;

sentences.zh: 親歿，善居喪，或廬於墓；

translations.literal: when parents died, one observed mourning well, sometimes dwelling in a hut by the tomb;
translations.idiomatic: when they died, one observed mourning properly, sometimes building a mourning hut beside the grave;

sentences.zh: 親遠行，萬里行求，或生還，或以喪歸。

translations.literal: when parents traveled far, one journeyed ten thousand li in search, sometimes bringing them back alive, sometimes returning with the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: when parents had gone far away, one traveled ten thousand li to seek them, sometimes bringing them home alive, sometimes returning with their remains.

sentences.zh: 友於兄弟，同居三五世以上，號義門，及諸義行，皆禮旌。

translations.literal: Fraternity among brothers, dwelling together for three to five generations or more, called "gates of righteousness," and all righteous acts were commended by ritual reward.
translations.idiomatic: Brotherly harmony, households living together for three to five generations or more and styled "gates of righteousness," and every other act of righteousness—all were honored by ritual commendation.

sentences.zh: 親病，刲股刳肝；

translations.literal: When parents were ill, cutting flesh from the thigh or excising the liver;
translations.idiomatic: When parents fell ill, cutting flesh from one's thigh or excising one's liver;

sentences.zh: 親喪，以身殉：皆以傷生有禁，有司以事聞，輒破格報可。

translations.literal: when parents died, dying with one's body: although harming one's life was forbidden, when officials reported such matters, approval was routinely granted as an exception.
translations.idiomatic: when parents died, giving one's life in their stead—although self-injury was prohibited by law, whenever officials reported such cases, exceptional approval was invariably granted.

sentences.zh: 所以教民者，若是其周其密也。

translations.literal: Thus the teaching of the people was so thorough and so meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the instruction of the people was carried to such thoroughness and such fineness.

sentences.zh: 國史承前例，撰次孝友傳，亦頗及諸義行。

translations.literal: The national history, following earlier precedent, compiled biographies of filial piety and fraternity, also treating various righteous acts at length.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic history, following earlier models, arranged biographies of filial sons and friendly brothers and also gave considerable attention to other righteous conduct.

sentences.zh: 合之方志甄錄、文家傳述，無慮千百人。

translations.literal: Combined with selections in local gazetteers and accounts by literary families, there were no fewer than a thousand or more.
translations.idiomatic: Together with what local gazetteers had selected and what literary families had recorded, there were certainly no fewer than a thousand such cases.

sentences.zh: 採其尤者，用沈約宋書例，為孝義傳。

translations.literal: Choosing the foremost among them, following Shen Yue's method in the Book of Song, they composed biographies of filial and righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From among them the most outstanding were chosen, and following Shen Yue's precedent in the Book of Song, biographies of filial and righteous conduct were written.

sentences.zh: 事親存沒能盡禮；

translations.literal: Serving parents in life and death with full observance of ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Those who served their parents with complete ritual propriety whether they lived or had died;

sentences.zh: 或遘家庭之變，能不失其正；

translations.literal: or encountering domestic upheaval yet not losing rectitude;
translations.idiomatic: or those who met upheaval within the family yet did not lose their moral footing;

sentences.zh: 或遇寇難、值水火，能全其親。

translations.literal: or meeting bandits and calamity, fire and flood, yet able to preserve their parents.
translations.idiomatic: or those who in the face of bandits, disaster, fire, or flood were able to save their parents whole.

sentences.zh: 若殉親而死，或為親復仇，友於兄弟，同居三五世以上，及凡有義行者，各以類聚。

translations.literal: Those who died with their parents, or avenged their parents, were fraternal among brothers, dwelt together for three to five generations or more, and all who had righteous conduct were each grouped by category.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died for their parents, or who avenged them, those who were devoted to brothers and lived together for three to five generations or more, and everyone who performed righteous acts were each gathered under its proper heading.

sentences.zh: 事同，以時次。

translations.literal: When the matter was the same, they were ordered by time.
translations.idiomatic: When the deeds were of the same kind, they were arranged in chronological order.

sentences.zh: 孝為二卷，友與義合一卷。

translations.literal: Filial piety formed two scrolls; fraternity and righteousness were combined in one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Filial conduct fills two scrolls; brotherly devotion and righteous conduct share one scroll together.

sentences.zh: 硃用純，字致一，江南崑山人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yongchun, style name Zhiyi, was a native of Kunshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yongchun, whose style was Zhiyi, came from Kunshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父集璜，明季以諸生死難。

translations.literal: His father Jihuang died in the calamity at the end of the Ming as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jihuang, a licentiate, perished in the dynastic collapse at the close of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 用純慕王裒攀柏之義，自號曰柏廬。

translations.literal: Yongchun admired Wang Pou's meaning in clinging to the cypress and styled himself Cypress Hut.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun admired Wang Pou's devotion among the cypress trees and took for himself the sobriquet Cypress Hut.

sentences.zh: 棄諸生，奉母。

translations.literal: He abandoned his status as licentiate and attended his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He gave up his licentiate standing and devoted himself to serving his mother.

sentences.zh: 其學確守程、硃，知行並進，而程於至敬。

translations.literal: His learning firmly upheld the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, advancing knowledge and action together, and he measured all things by utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he held fast to the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, advancing knowledge and practice together, and he took utmost reverence as his standard in all things.

sentences.zh: 來學者授以小學、近思錄。

translations.literal: Those who came to study he taught from the Elementary Learning and Reflections on Things at Hand.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came to him were instructed in the Elementary Learning and Reflections on Things at Hand.

sentences.zh: 仿白鹿洞規，設講約，從者皆興起。

translations.literal: Imitating the regulations of White Deer Grotto, he established lecture covenants, and all who followed were stirred to action.
translations.idiomatic: Following the White Deer Grotto regulations, he set up lecture covenants, and everyone who joined him was roused to earnest effort.

sentences.zh: 居喪哀毀，嘗曰：「宰我欲短喪，吾黨皆以為怪，然可見古人喪禮之盡，必蔬水饘粥哭泣哀毀無苟弛。

translations.literal: In mourning he was grief-stricken and emaciated. He once said: "Zai Wo wished to shorten mourning; our party all thought it strange, yet one can see how fully the ancients observed mourning ritual—they surely took only vegetables, water, and thin gruel, weeping and grieving without any careless relaxation.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning he was shattered by grief. He once said, "When Zai Wo wanted to shorten the mourning period, our school all thought it odd—but it shows how completely the ancients fulfilled mourning rites: only vegetables, water, and thin gruel, weeping and wasting away without the slightest careless slackening.

sentences.zh: 若今人飲酒食肉不改其常，雖更三年，豈謂久哉？

translations.literal: If people today drink wine and eat meat without changing their usual ways, even if three years pass, how can that be called long?"
translations.idiomatic: If people today drink wine and eat meat just as they always do, even if three years go by, what kind of mourning is that?"

sentences.zh: 」晚作輟講語，又為治家格言，語平易而切至。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote Words on Ceasing Lectures and also Maxims for Ordering the Household; the language was plain and to the point.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he wrote Words on Ceasing Lectures and also household maxims; his language was simple and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 病將革，設先人位，拜於堂，告無罪，顧弟子曰：「學問在性命，事業在忠孝。

translations.literal: When his illness was about to prove fatal, he set out the tablets of his forebears, bowed in the hall, declared himself without offense, turned to his disciples and said: "Learning lies in cultivating one's nature and life; achievement lies in loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness was nearing its end, he set out his ancestors' tablets, bowed in the hall, and declared himself free of guilt; then he turned to his disciples and said, "Scholarship rests in the cultivation of nature and life; true achievement rests in loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 」乃卒。

translations.literal: " Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he died.

sentences.zh: 用純與徐枋、楊無咎稱「吳中三高士」，皆明季死事之孤也。

translations.literal: Yongchun, together with Xu Fang and Yang Wujiu, were called "the three lofty scholars of Wu"; all were orphans of those who died for the cause at the end of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun, Xu Fang, and Yang Wujiu were known as "the three lofty scholars of Wu"; each was the son of a man who had died for the Ming cause.

sentences.zh: 吳蕃昌，字仲木，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Wu Fanchang, style name Zhongmu, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fanchang, whose style was Zhongmu, came from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父麟徵，明季死難，蕃昌事所後母查孝，居喪，水漿不入口。

translations.literal: His father Linzheng died in the calamity at the end of the Ming; Fanchang served his stepmother née Zha with filial piety, and in mourning he took neither water nor gruel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linzheng died in the Ming collapse; Fanchang served his stepmother, Lady Zha, with deep filial devotion, and during mourning he would not take even water or gruel.

sentences.zh: 既殯，啜粥，不茹蔬果。

translations.literal: After the encoffining he sipped only gruel and ate neither vegetables nor fruit.
translations.idiomatic: After the encoffining he took only thin gruel and would not eat vegetables or fruit.

sentences.zh: 寢苫，不脫衰絰。

translations.literal: He slept on rush matting and never removed his mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: He slept on a rush mat and never removed his mourning weeds.

sentences.zh: 比葬，嘔血數升，逾小祥遂卒。

translations.literal: By the time of burial he had vomited several sheng of blood; shortly after the lesser auspices he died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the burial he had vomited several sheng of blood; not long after the lesser mourning anniversary he died.

sentences.zh: 從弟謙牧，字裒仲。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Qian Mu, style name Baozhong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Qian Mu, whose style was Baozhong.

sentences.zh: 為程、硃之學。

translations.literal: He pursued the learning of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the learning of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 事母硃孝，居喪，杖不能起。

translations.literal: He served his mother née Zhu with filial piety; in mourning he was so weak he could not rise even with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother, Lady Zhu, with filial devotion; in mourning he was so frail he could not rise even with a staff.

sentences.zh: 疾稍間，手編父遺集，复困。

translations.literal: When his illness eased slightly, he compiled his father's posthumous writings by hand, then relapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness lifted a little, he set about editing his father's posthumous writings by hand, only to fall ill again.

sentences.zh: 治窀穸，哀動行路。

translations.literal: When he arranged the burial, his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared the burial, his grief moved everyone who passed along the road.

sentences.zh: 謙牧體素羸，益不自勝，遂卒。

translations.literal: Qian Mu's constitution had always been frail; he was ever less able to bear it, and so he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Mu had always been physically frail; he could bear no more and died.

sentences.zh: 蕃昌、謙牧皆交於張履祥，履祥稱之。

translations.literal: Fanchang and Qian Mu were both acquainted with Zhang Lüxiang, who praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Both Fanchang and Qian Mu were friends of Zhang Lüxiang, who spoke highly of them.

sentences.zh: 時以孝著者，復有歸安沈磊，亦履祥友也。

translations.literal: At the time one also famed for filial piety was Shen Lei of Gui'an, likewise a friend of Lüxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Another man of the time noted for filial piety was Shen Lei of Gui'an, who was also a friend of Zhang Lüxiang.

sentences.zh: 磊事母嚴，母不御酒肉，磊力請，終不聽。

translations.literal: Lei served his mother strictly; his mother would not partake of wine or meat, and though Lei earnestly pleaded, she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lei was strict in serving his mother; she would not touch wine or meat, and though he pleaded earnestly, she never yielded.

sentences.zh: 有疾，醫為言，乃御酒肉。

translations.literal: When she fell ill, the physician spoke on her behalf, and only then did she partake of wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill, the physician persuaded her, and only then would she take wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 磊客授於外，弟子具時食，不忍食，以為母未嘗也。

translations.literal: Lei taught pupils while lodging away from home; when disciples prepared his meal he could not bear to eat, thinking his mother had not yet tasted it.
translations.idiomatic: Lei taught students while living away from home; when his pupils set out his meal he could not bring himself to eat, for he thought his mother had not yet tasted such food.

sentences.zh: 弟子乃先以饋母，曰：「太君食矣。

translations.literal: The disciples then first sent food to his mother and said: "The lady has eaten."
translations.idiomatic: His pupils would first send food to his mother and then tell him, "Your mother has eaten."

sentences.zh: 」乃食，率以為常。

translations.literal: " Only then would he eat; this became his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then would he eat; this became his regular habit.

sentences.zh: 周靖，江南吳縣人。

translations.literal: Zhou Jing was a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing came from Wu County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父茂蘭，刺血上書明父順昌冤，事具明史。

translations.literal: His father Maolan wrote a petition in his own blood to clear the injustice done to his father Zhou Shunchang; the affair is fully recorded in the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maolan wrote a blood petition to vindicate his own father Zhou Shunchang; the full account appears in the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 靖少補諸生，事親能盡力。

translations.literal: Jing in his youth received appointment as licentiate and served his parents with full exertion.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jing was appointed licentiate and served his parents with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 茂蘭卒，擗踴哭泣，喪葬悉如禮。

translations.literal: When Maolan died, Jing beat his breast and stamped, weeping; the funeral and burial were entirely according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Maolan died, Jing beat his breast and wept aloud; the funeral and burial were conducted entirely according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 三年不脫衰絰，不飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: For three years he did not remove his mourning garments and did not drink wine or eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: For three years he never removed his mourning weeds and took neither wine nor meat.

sentences.zh: 小祥，有疾作，或謂在禮得飲酒食肉，靖不可。

translations.literal: At the lesser auspices an illness arose; some said that by ritual he might drink wine and eat meat, but Jing would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: At the lesser mourning anniversary he fell ill; some said ritual now permitted wine and meat, but Jing would not agree.

sentences.zh: 靖素善作篆，或請題榜，亦以喪辭。

translations.literal: Jing had always been skilled at seal script; when some asked him to inscribe a placard, he also declined on grounds of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was skilled in seal script; when people asked him to write inscriptions, he likewise refused on account of mourning.

sentences.zh: 耿燿，河南太康人。

translations.literal: Geng Yao was a native of Taikang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yao came from Taikang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 世農。

translations.literal: His family were farmers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 父應科，好施與，七世同居，顏其堂曰「效藝」。

translations.literal: His father Yingke was fond of giving and bestowing; seven generations dwelt together, and he inscribed their hall "Following the Arts."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingke was generous in giving; seven generations lived under one roof, and he named their hall Following the Arts.

sentences.zh: 兄光，明諸生，孝後母而教諸弟嚴，燿從之學，事必諮而後行。

translations.literal: His elder brother Guang was a Ming licentiate, filial to his stepmother and strict in teaching his younger brothers; Yao studied under him and would consult before acting in any matter.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Guang, a Ming licentiate, was filial to their stepmother and stern in instructing the younger brothers; Yao studied under him and would consult Guang before undertaking anything.

sentences.zh: 明末，流寇屠太康，燿與弟炳舁母避河北，貿布以養。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, roaming bandits massacred Taikang; Yao and his younger brother Bing carried their mother on their shoulders to flee north of the Yellow River and traded in cloth to support her.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Ming, bandits ravaged Taikang; Yao and his younger brother Bing shouldered their mother and fled north of the Yellow River, trading in cloth to support her.

sentences.zh: 母病，朝出暮歸，不解帶累月。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, he went out at dawn and returned at dusk, not loosening his belt for months on end.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he went out at dawn and returned at dusk, going for months without even loosening his belt.

sentences.zh: 母卒，挽車歸母喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he drew the cart to bring her coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he himself drew the cart that bore her coffin home.

sentences.zh: 炳亦純謹，定興耿權與弟極以孝友聞，炳慕其為人，分田舍處之，孫奇逢為作三耿傳焉。

translations.literal: Bing was also pure and careful; Geng Quan of Dingxing and his younger brother Ji were famed for filial piety and fraternity; Bing admired their conduct, divided fields and dwellings to house them, and Sun Qifeng wrote a biography of the three Gengs.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was likewise upright and careful. Geng Quan of Dingxing and his brother Ji were renowned for filial devotion and brotherly harmony; Bing admired them, divided fields and houses to lodge them, and Sun Qifeng wrote a joint biography of the three Geng brothers.

sentences.zh: 方寇至，光前卒，未葬，子於彝號泣守其柩不去，寇執之，推隕城下，傷腰膂，幾死。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, Guang had died earlier and was not yet buried; his son Yu Yi wailed and guarded the coffin without leaving; the bandits seized him, pushed him off the city wall, injuring his loins and back, nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came, Guang had already died and lay unburied; his son Yu Yi wept and would not leave the coffin. The bandits seized him and hurled him from the wall, injuring his back and sides so severely that he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 寇退，歸掬土掩柩乃去。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, he returned, scooped earth to cover the coffin, and only then departed.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits withdrew, he came back, heaped earth over the coffin with his hands, and only then left.

sentences.zh: 縣飢，知縣餽以粟，散贍貧乏。

translations.literal: When the county suffered famine, the magistrate presented him with grain, which he distributed to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: During a county famine the magistrate gave him grain, which he distributed to support the destitute.

sentences.zh: 督僮蔬，任飢者刈以食。

translations.literal: He had his servants plant vegetables and allowed the hungry to reap them for food.
translations.idiomatic: He had his servants plant vegetables and let the hungry harvest them for food.

sentences.zh: 同時有耿輔，虞城人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Geng Fu, a native of Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Geng Fu of Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 奉母避寇開封，寇決河灌城，倚浮木負母以渡。

translations.literal: He attended his mother in fleeing bandits to Kaifeng; the bandits breached the river to flood the city, and leaning on a floating log he carried his mother across.
translations.idiomatic: He took his mother to Kaifeng to escape the bandits; when they breached the dikes and flooded the city, he bore her across on a floating log.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀毀，緇衣粗食終其世。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was grief-stricken and emaciated, wearing black garments and coarse food for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he was shattered by grief; he wore plain black clothes and ate coarse food for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 李景濂，字亦週，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Li Jinglian, style name Yizhou, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglian, whose style was Yizhou, came from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幼喪母，父再娶於何而卒。

translations.literal: He lost his mother in childhood; his father remarried a woman of the He clan and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother while still young; his father remarried a woman of the He clan and then died.

sentences.zh: 何年少，媒氏欲奪之，景濂聞，伺於道，出椎擊之，歸告何。

translations.literal: He was still young; a matchmaker wished to take her away; Jinglian heard of it, waited on the road, came out with a mallet and struck him, then returned and told Lady He.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He was still young; a matchmaker tried to take her away. Jinglian heard of it, lay in wait on the road, struck the man with a mallet, and went home to tell Lady He.

sentences.zh: 何相與慟哭，誓相依終身。

translations.literal: He and Lady He wept together and vowed to rely on each other for life.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lady He wept together and swore to depend on each other for the rest of their lives.

sentences.zh: 何教景濂嚴，景濂事何甚謹。

translations.literal: Lady He taught Jinglian strictly, and Jinglian served Lady He with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He raised him strictly, and he served her with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 何嗜酪，景濂日入市求之，端捧急趨，如鳥張翼。

translations.literal: Lady He loved curds; Jinglian went to market daily to seek them, holding the bowl level and hurrying along like a bird spreading its wings.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He loved curds; every day Jinglian went to market for them, holding the bowl steady and hurrying along with arms spread like wings.

sentences.zh: 市人怪而求其故，則皆歎其孝，為讓道。

translations.literal: Market people wondered and asked the reason; when they learned it, all sighed at his filial piety and made way for him.
translations.idiomatic: People in the market wondered and asked why; when they learned the reason, they all marveled at his filial devotion and cleared a path for him.

sentences.zh: 何老病，景濂侍疾七年不怠。

translations.literal: When Lady He grew old and ill, Jinglian attended her sickness for seven years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady He grew old and fell ill, Jinglian nursed her for seven years without slackening.

sentences.zh: 何卒，景濂亦六十，廬墓三年，作孺子泣。

translations.literal: When Lady He died, Jinglian was also sixty; he dwelt in a hut by the tomb for three years and composed Lament of an Infant's Weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady He died, Jinglian was himself sixty; he lived in a mourning hut by her grave for three years and wrote Lament of an Infant's Weeping.

sentences.zh: 景濂明諸生，明亡，棄諸生去為醫。

translations.literal: Jinglian had been a Ming licentiate; when the Ming perished he abandoned his licentiate status and became a physician.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglian had been a Ming licentiate; when the dynasty fell he gave up that standing and took up medicine.

sentences.zh: 汪灝，江南休寧人。

translations.literal: Wang Hao was a native of Xiuning in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao came from Xiuning in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 晨、日昂、日昇，其弟也。

translations.literal: Chen, Ri'ang, and Risheng were his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, Ri'ang, and Risheng were his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 父病咯血，灝年十六，割股和藥進，良愈。

translations.literal: When his father was ill with spitting blood, Hao at age sixteen cut flesh from his thigh, mixed it with medicine, and presented it; his father recovered well.
translations.idiomatic: When his father coughed blood, the sixteen-year-old Hao cut flesh from his thigh, mixed it into medicine, and gave it to him; his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 後數年病足，晨割股煉為末，敷治亦愈。

translations.literal: Several years later his father was ill in the foot; Chen cut flesh from his thigh, refined it to powder, applied it as treatment, and he also recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, when his father suffered from a foot ailment, Chen cut flesh from his thigh, refined it to powder, applied it as a poultice, and he recovered as well.

sentences.zh: 又數年復咯血，晨复割臂以療。

translations.literal: Several years later he again spat blood; Chen again cut flesh from his arm to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the coughing of blood returned; Chen again cut flesh from his arm to heal him.

sentences.zh: 更數年，疾大作，灝复割臂，勿瘳。

translations.literal: After several more years, the illness grew severe; Hao again cut flesh from his arm, but it did not heal.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the sickness worsened sharply; Hao cut flesh from his arm once more, yet his father did not recover.

sentences.zh: 晨病，日昂泣曰：「吾兄割臂愈父，吾不能割以愈吾兄乎？

translations.literal: Chen fell ill; Ri'ang wept and said, "My elder brother cut his arm to heal Father—can I not cut mine to heal my elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell ill, Ri'ang wept and said, "My brother cut his arm to save our father—why shouldn't I cut mine to save my brother?"

sentences.zh: 」眾尼之。

translations.literal: The crowd restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone held him back.

sentences.zh: 懵且僕，匠治棺，日昇持匠斧斷指，血淋漓，調藥以飲晨。

translations.literal: Chen was dazed and prostrate; a carpenter was building a coffin. Risheng took the carpenter's axe and severed his finger; blood poured forth, and he mixed medicine for Chen to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Chen lay dazed and collapsed while a carpenter worked on a coffin. Risheng seized the carpenter's axe and cut off his finger; blood streaming down, he prepared medicine and gave it to Chen to drink.

sentences.zh: 有司表其門曰「一門四孝友」。

translations.literal: The local officials honored their gate with a placard reading "One Household of Four Filial Brothers."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities posted an honorary tablet at their gate proclaiming "One Family, Four Filial Brothers."

sentences.zh: 錢塘吳瑗及弟琦、璠、琰相友愛，年皆逾九十。

translations.literal: Wu Yuan of Qiantang and his younger brothers Qi, Fan, and Yan loved one another mutually; all were over ninety years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuan of Qiantang and his brothers Qi, Fan, and Yan were deeply devoted to one another; each lived past ninety.

sentences.zh: 江蘇華亭姜應龍，應龍子世璜，世璜子文樞，文樞子超萃，超萃子懷權，懷權子栻，六世皆以孝行旌，人尤以為難。

translations.literal: Jiang Yinglong of Huating in Jiangsu—Yinglong's son Shihuang, Shihuang's son Wenshu, Wenshu's son Chaoqi, Chaoqi's son Huaiquan, Huaiquan's son Shi—for six generations all were commended for filial conduct, and people regarded this as especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yinglong of Huating, Jiangsu, was followed by a line of filial heirs—his son Shihuang, then Wenshu, Chaoqi, Huaiquan, and Shi—for six generations honored for filial conduct, a feat people considered exceptionally rare.

sentences.zh: 黃農，江南元和人。

translations.literal: Huang Nong was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Nong came from Yuanhe in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父袞，諸生。

translations.literal: His father Gun was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gun had been a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 農年十餘，母吳病六年，農侍疾不懈。

translations.literal: Nong was just over ten; his mother Lady Wu was ill for six years, and Nong attended her sickness without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong was in his early teens, his mother Lady Wu fell ill for six years; he nursed her without ever letting up.

sentences.zh: 母卒，慟屢絕，坐臥母柩側。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he sobbed until he repeatedly fainted, sitting and lying beside her coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, he wept until he lost consciousness again and again, refusing to leave her coffin day or night.

sentences.zh: 袞客授於外，攜農俱。

translations.literal: Gun taught students as a guest instructor elsewhere and took Nong along.
translations.idiomatic: Gun taught as a hired tutor away from home and brought Nong with him.

sentences.zh: 久之，察其枕漬淚若膏，貌癯然如初喪。

translations.literal: After a long while, he observed that his pillow was soaked with tears like grease, and his appearance was gaunt as if in fresh mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gun noticed that the boy's pillow was soaked with tears and that he looked as thin and grief-stricken as if his mother had just died.

sentences.zh: 袞客授稍遠家，農歸，五日一往省，袞止之，則私伺門外問安否，衣服器用，時其寒暑具以往。

translations.literal: When Gun's guest teaching took him somewhat farther from home, Nong would return every five days to visit; Gun forbade this, so he would secretly wait outside the door to ask after his well-being, bringing clothing and utensils suited to the season.
translations.idiomatic: When Gun took a post farther from home, Nong came back every five days to check on him. Gun forbade it, so the boy would linger outside the door instead, asking after his father's health and sending in clothing and supplies according to the season.

sentences.zh: 一夕，心悸，走省，袞得暴疾，舁以歸。

translations.literal: One night his heart palpitated; he ran to visit and found Gun stricken with sudden illness; they carried him home.
translations.idiomatic: One night a sudden dread seized him; he rushed to see his father and found Gun stricken with a sudden illness, so they carried him home.

sentences.zh: 會除夕禱神，原減算益父，袞愈。

translations.literal: It happened to be New Year's Eve; he prayed to the gods, vowing to shorten his own lifespan to extend his father's; Gun recovered.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve he prayed to the gods, offering to shorten his own life in exchange for his father's; Gun recovered.

sentences.zh: 農三十餘而卒，妻金，亦賢孝。

translations.literal: Nong died in his thirties; his wife, surnamed Jin, was also virtuous and filial.
translations.idiomatic: Nong died in his thirties; his wife, Lady Jin, was likewise virtuous and devoted.

sentences.zh: 曹亨，陝西鎮安人。

translations.literal: Cao Heng was a native of Zhen'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Heng came from Zhen'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 年十一喪母，不能具棺，號泣於路，乞自鬻為斂。

translations.literal: At age eleven he lost his mother; unable to afford a coffin, he wailed on the road, begging to sell himself to pay for burial.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at eleven; too poor to afford a coffin, he wept in the streets, offering to sell himself into bondage to pay for her burial.

sentences.zh: 或與之金，葬母畢，即詣其家執役終身。

translations.literal: Someone gave him money; after burying his mother he went straight to that person's home and served as a bondsman for life.
translations.idiomatic: A benefactor gave him the money; once his mother was buried, he went to that man's home and served him for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 黃嘉章，湖南桂陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Jiazhang was a native of Guiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jiazhang came from Guiyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂之亂，從父避兵連珠崖。

translations.literal: During Wu Sangui's rebellion, he followed his father to flee the warfare to Lianzhuyan.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu Sangui's rebellion, he fled with his father to Lianzhuyan to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 父歿，兄嘉林年十六，嘉章亦年十一，自鬻以葬父。

translations.literal: When his father died, his elder brother Jialin was sixteen and Jiazhang was also eleven; he sold himself to bury his father.
translations.idiomatic: When their father died, Jialin was sixteen and Jiazhang only eleven; Jiazhang sold himself into servitude to pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 嘉林稍長，力為傭，得錢贖嘉章還，兄弟相友愛。

translations.literal: When Jialin grew somewhat older, he worked hard as a hired laborer, earned money to redeem Jiazhang and bring him back; the brothers loved one another mutually.
translations.idiomatic: As Jialin matured, he worked as a hired laborer, saved enough to buy his brother's freedom, and the two remained devoted to each other.

sentences.zh: 鄭明允，江南歙縣人。

translations.literal: Zheng Mingyun was a native of She County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mingyun came from She County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，耿精忠兵至，明允侍母抱譜牒及先世遺筆入山。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi era, when Geng Jingzhong's troops arrived, Mingyun attended his mother, carrying genealogical records and ancestral writings into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign, when Geng Jingzhong's soldiers arrived, Mingyun escorted his mother into the mountains, clutching the family genealogy and his ancestors' writings.

sentences.zh: 賊大索山中，明允夜負母匿僻塢，還挈二子，未至，霧溢山，虎聲震林木，納二子石穴中，疾趨侍母。

translations.literal: The rebels searched the mountains thoroughly; Mingyun by night carried his mother and hid in a secluded ravine, then went back to fetch his two sons; before he reached them, mist filled the mountains and tiger roars shook the trees; he placed the two sons in a stone cave and hurried to attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel troops scoured the mountains, Mingyun carried his mother under cover of night to a hidden ravine, then returned for his two sons. Before he reached them, fog rolled over the hills and tiger roars shook the forest; he hid the boys in a stone cave and raced back to his mother.

sentences.zh: 賊退，二子亦無恙。

translations.literal: When the rebels withdrew, the two sons were also unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew, both sons emerged unscathed.

sentences.zh: 兄病，視湯藥不去側。

translations.literal: When his elder brother fell ill, he watched over medicines and never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother fell ill, he tended his medicine and never left the bedside.

sentences.zh: 及亡，每慟輒絕。

translations.literal: When he died, each time he mourned he would faint.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, each burst of grief left him unconscious.

sentences.zh: 與其戚同賈，失其貲，明允發橐金盡與之。

translations.literal: A kinsman went into trade with him and lost his capital; Mingyun opened his purse and gave him everything.
translations.idiomatic: A relative who had gone into business with him lost his stake; Mingyun emptied his purse and gave him the entire sum.

sentences.zh: 族子縊客舍，明允為坐守達曙，白於官，出私財以斂。

translations.literal: A clansman's son hanged himself at an inn; Mingyun sat keeping watch until dawn, reported to the authorities, and paid from private funds for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When a clansman's son hanged himself at an inn, Mingyun kept vigil until dawn, notified the authorities, and paid for the burial out of his own pocket.

sentences.zh: 有友盪其貲，困甚，明允罄所有佽之，無難色。

translations.literal: A friend squandered his capital and was deeply distressed; Mingyun emptied all he had to assist him, without any sign of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: When a friend squandered his savings and fell into dire need, Mingyun gave him everything he owned without a moment's hesitation.

sentences.zh: 明允世業醫，精而不試，曰：「十得九，猶有一誤。

translations.literal: Mingyun's family profession was medicine; he was skilled but did not practice, saying, "Nine out of ten succeed, yet there is still one mistake."
translations.idiomatic: His family were physicians by trade; though skilled, he refused to practice, saying, "Even when nine of ten patients recover, one still errs."

sentences.zh: 」業賈終其身。

translations.literal: He pursued trade all his life.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his entire life in commerce instead.

sentences.zh: 劉宗洙，字長源；

translations.literal: Liu Zongzhu, styled Changyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhu, whose style was Changyuan;

sentences.zh: 弟恩廣，字錫三：湖北襄城人。

translations.literal: his younger brother Enguang, styled Xisan: natives of Xiangcheng in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: and his younger brother Enguang, styled Xisan—they came from Xiangcheng in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 父漢臣，明季從軍。

translations.literal: Their father Hanchen joined the army in the late Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Hanchen had served in the army in the waning years of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 襄城破，被數創，幾殆。

translations.literal: When Xiangcheng fell, he suffered many wounds and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangcheng fell, he was badly wounded and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 恩廣兩耳斷，號泣負以歸。

translations.literal: Enguang, with both ears severed, wept and wailing carried him home on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Enguang, his ears cut off in the fighting, carried his father home on his back, weeping all the way.

sentences.zh: 宗洙方走避寇，聞父難，往赴，賊截其耳鼻。

translations.literal: Zongzhu had been fleeing the bandits; hearing of his father's plight, he set out to help, and the bandits cut off his nose and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhu was fleeing the rebels when he heard of his father's danger; he rushed to help, and the rebels cut off his nose and ears.

sentences.zh: 居數年，父病，嘗糞，時稱襄城「嘗糞孝子」。

translations.literal: Several years later, when their father fell ill, they tasted his feces; at the time they were called Xiangcheng's "Taste-Feces Filial Sons."
translations.idiomatic: Years later, when their father fell ill, they tasted his stool to gauge his condition; people called them Xiangcheng's "Filial Sons Who Tasted Feces."

sentences.zh: 父歾，與季弟宗泗同居，俄與恩廣皆得官，以母老不出。

translations.literal: When their father died, he lived with his youngest brother Zongsi; soon both Zongzhu and Enguang received official posts but did not take them because their mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: After their father died, Zongzhu lived with his youngest brother Zongsi; soon both he and Enguang were offered official posts, but they declined because their mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 母歾，恩廣嘔血至篤疾。

translations.literal: When their mother died, Enguang vomited blood until grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: When their mother died, Enguang vomited blood until he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 或慰解，曰：「勿復言，五內裂矣！

translations.literal: Someone tried to comfort him; he said, "Do not speak again—my five viscera are torn apart!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone tried to console him, he said, "Say no more—my heart is torn to pieces!"

sentences.zh: 」遂卒。

translations.literal: And he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 宗洙積哀兼痛弟，亦嘔血卒。

translations.literal: Zongzhu accumulated grief together with pain for his brother and also vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhu, grief upon grief for his brother, also vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 恩廣子青藜，康熙四十五年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Enguang's son Qingli passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi and was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Enguang's son Qingli became a jinshi in 1706 and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，哀毀嘔血，事母不復出。

translations.literal: Upon his father's mourning, grief-stricken he vomited blood and served his mother without going out again.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, grief left him vomiting blood; he stayed home to care for his mother and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 何復漢，江西廣昌人。

translations.literal: He Fuhan was a native of Guangchang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He Fuhan came from Guangchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十五而喪父，哭淚皆血。

translations.literal: At fifteen he lost his father; his weeping tears were all blood.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at fifteen and wept until his tears ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 長事母孝，母疾作，嘗糞苦甘以測病深淺，不解帶者數月。

translations.literal: Growing up he served his mother filially; when her illness flared, he tasted her feces for bitterness or sweetness to gauge the depth of the sickness, and for months did not undo his belt.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he cared for his mother with deep devotion; when she fell ill, he tasted her stool to judge whether the illness was worsening, and for months never undressed for sleep.

sentences.zh: 母歾，寢苫三月，淚漬苫左右盡血痕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he slept on the mourning mat for three months; tears soaked the mat on both sides entirely with blood traces.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, he slept on a straw mourning mat for three months; tears soaked both sides of the mat with bloodstains.

sentences.zh: 葬，乃廬墓側，日夜悲號，喪終猶廬居。

translations.literal: After burial he built a hut beside the tomb, wailing day and night; when the mourning period ended he still lived in the hut.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he built a hut beside the grave and wailed day and night; even when the mourning period ended, he continued to live there.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠兵至，复漢守墓不去，親知毀其廬，乃哭而行。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong's troops arrived, Fuhan guarded the tomb and would not leave; relatives and friends destroyed his hut, so he wept and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong's soldiers arrived, Fuhan refused to leave the grave; relatives and friends tore down his hut, and he left in tears.

sentences.zh: 著古今粹言示子孫。

translations.literal: He authored Gǔjīn Cuìyán to instruct his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Gǔjīn Cuìyán as a moral guide for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 子人龍，康熙五十二年進士，入翰林。

translations.literal: His son Renlong passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-second year of Kangxi and entered the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renlong became a jinshi in 1713 and joined the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 許季覺，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Xu Jijue was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jijue came from Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少尚俠，既折節讀書。

translations.literal: In youth he admired chivalry; afterward he reformed himself and took up study.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he admired bold chivalry; later he reformed himself and devoted himself to books.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，水漿不入口者七日，杖而後起。

translations.literal: During mourning for his parents, he took neither water nor food for seven days and only rose afterward leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his parents, he took neither food nor drink for seven days and could rise only with the help of a staff.

sentences.zh: 含殮、殯葬、虞祔、卒哭、祥禫皆用古禮。

translations.literal: Encoffining, burial, yufu, zucu, xiang, and chan all followed ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: Encoffining, burial, yufu, zucu, xiang, and chan were all performed according to ancient rites.

sentences.zh: 葬，躬負土，廬於側，朝夕哭不輟。

translations.literal: At burial he personally carried earth; he built a hut beside the tomb and wept morning and evening without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial he carried earth on his own back, built a hut beside the grave, and wept morning and evening without stopping.

sentences.zh: 季覺故與同縣查氏交密，查氏貴，營葬侵許氏墓地。

translations.literal: Jijue had formerly been on close terms with the Zha clan of the same county; the Zha grew prestigious, and their burial arrangements encroached on Xu clan grave land.
translations.idiomatic: Jijue had once been close friends with the Zha clan of his county; when the Zha family rose in status, their burial plans encroached on Xu family grave land.

sentences.zh: 季覺曰：「吾不能以友賣親。

translations.literal: Jijue said, "I cannot sell my kin for the sake of friendship."
translations.idiomatic: Jijue said, "I will not betray my family's interests for the sake of a friend."

sentences.zh: 」訟連年不決，親朋居間，季覺終不讓。

translations.literal: The lawsuit went unresolved for years; relatives and friends mediated, but Jijue never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The lawsuit dragged on for years; friends and relatives tried to mediate, but Jijue never backed down.

sentences.zh: 查氏誣季覺通海，逮獄，有為辨者，獄稍解，避地山陰。

translations.literal: The Zha clan accused Jijue of colluding with pirates; he was arrested and imprisoned; someone pleaded on his behalf, the case was somewhat resolved, and he fled to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zha clan accused him of colluding with pirates and had him thrown in prison; after someone spoke in his defense and the case eased, he fled to Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 查氏复誣以他事，再逮獄。

translations.literal: The Zha clan again accused him on other grounds, and he was arrested and imprisoned once more.
translations.idiomatic: The Zha clan accused him again on other charges, and he was thrown back in prison.

sentences.zh: 季覺度不免，獄中碎瓷盎吞之，死。

translations.literal: Jijue judged that he could not escape; in prison he smashed a ceramic bowl and swallowed the shards, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no way out, Jijue smashed a ceramic bowl in his cell, swallowed the shards, and died.

sentences.zh: 吳氏四孝子，江南崇明人，失其名。

translations.literal: The four filial sons of the Wu clan, natives of Chongming in Jiangnan, have lost their names.
translations.idiomatic: The four filial sons of the Wu clan came from Chongming in Jiangnan; their names are no longer known.

sentences.zh: 父壯年家貧，鬻子為富家奴。

translations.literal: Their father in his prime years was poor and sold his sons as slaves to a wealthy family.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his prime their father was so poor that he sold his sons as slaves to a wealthy household.

sentences.zh: 及長，皆能自贖。

translations.literal: When they grew up, all were able to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When they came of age, each managed to buy back his freedom.

sentences.zh: 娶婦列肆居，養父母，兄弟議奉父母膳，月而易。

translations.literal: They married, set up shops, and lived separately while supporting their parents; the brothers discussed serving their parents' meals, rotating monthly.
translations.idiomatic: After marrying, they opened shops and lived nearby while supporting their parents; the brothers agreed to take turns providing their meals, rotating each month.

sentences.zh: 諸婦曰：「翁姑老矣！

translations.literal: The daughters-in-law said, "Father-in-law and mother-in-law are old!"
translations.idiomatic: Their wives objected: "Our in-laws are elderly!"

sentences.zh: 月而易，必三月後方為翁姑具膳，太疏。

translations.literal: With monthly rotation, it would be three months before meals were prepared for the in-laws—too sparse.
translations.idiomatic: If we rotate by the month, each of them would wait three months between proper meals—that is far too infrequent.

sentences.zh: 」复議日而易，諸婦又曰：「翁姑老矣！

translations.literal: They discussed rotating daily; the daughters-in-law again said, "Father-in-law and mother-in-law are old!"
translations.idiomatic: They tried daily rotation instead, but the wives protested again: "Our in-laws are elderly!"

sentences.zh: 日而易，必三日後方為翁姑具膳，仍太疏。

translations.literal: With daily rotation, it would still be three days before meals were prepared for the in-laws—still too sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Even with daily rotation, each would still wait three days between proper meals—that is still too infrequent.

sentences.zh: 」乃議伯具早餐，仲午，叔脯，次日季具早餐，周而復始。

translations.literal: So they agreed that the eldest would provide breakfast, the second lunch, the third dinner; the next day the youngest would provide breakfast, and the cycle would repeat.
translations.idiomatic: They settled on a plan: the eldest son would provide breakfast, the second lunch, the third dinner; the next day the youngest would provide breakfast, and so on in rotation.

sentences.zh: 越五日，諸子合具饌奉父母，子孫皆侍，諸婦以次上酒食，以為常。

translations.literal: Every five days all the sons together prepared a feast for their parents; descendants all attended, and the daughters-in-law served food and drink in turn—this became the custom.
translations.idiomatic: Every five days all the sons would prepare a joint feast for their parents; the whole family gathered, and the daughters-in-law served food and drink in turn—a practice they kept for life.

sentences.zh: 室置★，兄弟各具錢五十，父食畢，取錢入市嬉，易果餌，歸畀諸孫，錢將盡，复具。

translations.literal: They placed a coffer in the room; each brother contributed fifty coins. After their father finished eating, he would take the money to amuse himself in the market, exchange it for sweets, and give them to his grandchildren; when the money was nearly gone, they would replenish it.
translations.idiomatic: They kept a money chest in the house; each brother put in fifty coins. After meals their father would take the coins to the market for amusement, buy sweets, and bring them home for his grandchildren; when the coins ran low, the brothers refilled the chest.

sentences.zh: 父或從博徒戲，兄弟潛以錢畀博徒，令陽負與其父以為歡。

translations.literal: When their father sometimes gambled with gamblers, the brothers secretly gave money to the gamblers and had them pretend to lose to their father for his delight.
translations.idiomatic: When their father gambled with local players, the brothers secretly paid the gamblers to lose on purpose so their father would win and be pleased.

sentences.zh: 行之數十年，父母皆將百歲，奉事不衰。

translations.literal: They practiced this for several decades; both parents were nearly a hundred years old, and their service never declined.
translations.idiomatic: They kept this up for decades; both parents lived to nearly a hundred, and their devotion never waned.

sentences.zh: 陸隴其為之傳。

translations.literal: Lu Longqi wrote their biography.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Longqi wrote a biography of them.

sentences.zh: 雷顯宗，河南陳州人。

translations.literal: Lei Xianzong was a native of Chenzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Xianzong came from Chenzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held licentiate rank.

sentences.zh: 父病瘓，顯宗摩掌熱拊父四支，二十七晝夜不倦，父良愈。

translations.literal: When his father was ill with paralysis, Xianzong rubbed his palms warm and patted his father's four limbs for twenty-seven days and nights without tiring; his father recovered well.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell paralyzed, Xianzong warmed his hands and massaged his father's limbs for twenty-seven days and nights without rest; his father made a full recovery.

sentences.zh: 居數年，复病劇，侍湯藥兩月餘，竟卒，哀毀柴立。

translations.literal: Several years later he fell severely ill again; Xianzong attended his medicines for more than two months, but he died in the end; grief left Xianzong emaciated as a withered stalk.
translations.idiomatic: Years later his father fell gravely ill again; Xianzong nursed him for more than two months, but he died; grief left Xianzong wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 居母喪亦如之。

translations.literal: At his mother's mourning he did the same.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother with equal devotion.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，歲饑，出米粟濟貧乏，代償其逋賦。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi era, in years of famine he distributed grain and millet to relieve the poor and paid their tax arrears on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign, when famine struck he gave out grain to the poor and paid their overdue taxes for them.

sentences.zh: 有鬻其孥者，贖以歸。

translations.literal: Those who had sold their wives and children, he redeemed and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: When families had sold wives or children, he bought them back and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 佽婚葬者三百餘家。

translations.literal: He assisted with weddings and funerals for more than three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He helped more than three hundred families pay for weddings and funerals.

sentences.zh: 顯宗年九十，朔望集家人講孝經、曲禮、內則諸篇，裡閈稱其家範。

translations.literal: At ninety years of age, Xianzong gathered his family on the new and full moons to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Quli, the Neize, and other chapters; the neighborhood praised his household as a model.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety, Xianzong gathered his family on the first and fifteenth of each month to read from the Classic of Filial Piety, the Quli, the Neize, and related texts; neighbors hailed his household as a model of propriety.

sentences.zh: 趙清，山東諸城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Qing was a native of Zhucheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qing came from Zhucheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 生有至性，嗜酒，與同縣李澄中、劉翼明輩遍陟縣中山，縱飲，輒沉頓。

translations.literal: Born with utmost nature, he loved wine; with Li Chengzhong, Liu Yiming, and others of the same county he climbed every hill in the county, drank freely, and always passed out drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He had an intensely passionate nature and loved wine; with Li Chengzhong, Liu Yiming, and other county friends he climbed every hill around Zhucheng, drinking hard until he passed out.

sentences.zh: 喪父，廬墓側百日，母往攜以歸。

translations.literal: When his father died, he built a hut beside the tomb for a hundred days; his mother came and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he lived in a hut by the grave for a hundred days until his mother came and took him home.

sentences.zh: 喪母，复廬墓側，麻衣躬畚鍤，負土為墳，毀幾殆。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he again built a hut beside the tomb, wore hemp mourning clothes, personally wielded basket and spade, and carried earth to build the mound; grief nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he again lived beside the grave in hemp mourning clothes, digging and carrying earth to build the mound himself until grief nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 客有勸者，清曰：「清所以為此者，蓋下愚居喪法耳。

translations.literal: A guest tried to advise him; Qing said, "The reason Qing does this is merely the method of mourning for the utterly dull-witted."
translations.idiomatic: When a visitor tried to dissuade him, Qing said, "I do this because it is the mourning practice of the simplest fool."

sentences.zh: 清狂盪如湍水，不居墓側，將食旨，久而甘；

translations.literal: Qing is wild and unrestrained like rushing water; if he does not dwell beside the tomb, he will eat delicacies and in time find them sweet;
translations.idiomatic: I am wild and ungovernable as a torrent; if I do not stay beside the grave, I will eat fine food and in time find it sweet;

sentences.zh: 聞樂，久而樂；

translations.literal: hear music, and in time find it pleasurable;
translations.idiomatic: hear music and in time enjoy it;

sentences.zh: 居處，且久而安。

translations.literal: live in comfort, and in time feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: live in comfort and in time feel content.

sentences.zh: 不一期，沉湎不可問矣。

translations.literal: Before one year had passed, he was sunk in indulgence beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he had sunk back into dissipation beyond recall.

sentences.zh: 不孝孰甚！

translations.literal: What unfilial conduct could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: What could be more unfilial than that!

sentences.zh: 」居廬久，或傳有狼與犬為守廬，狎不相齧也。

translations.literal: " After he had lived in the hut a long time, some reported that a wolf and a dog together guarded the hut, tame and not biting each other.
translations.idiomatic: After he had lived in the mourning hut for a long while, people said a wolf and a dog both stood guard and lived together without biting one another.

sentences.zh: 榮漣，江南無錫人。

translations.literal: Rong Lian was a native of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lian came from Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，多病，母令為道士。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and often ill, his mother had him become a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father young and was often sick; his mother had him enter the Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 善詩畫。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in both poetry and painting.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，出游得珍玩、良藥必以奉母。

translations.literal: Filial in serving his mother, whenever he traveled and obtained rare curios or fine medicines he always presented them to her.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother filially; on his travels, any rare treasure or good medicine he obtained he brought home for her.

sentences.zh: 遊倦歸，晨昏侍母側。

translations.literal: When weary of traveling he returned and attended her morning and evening at her side.
translations.idiomatic: When travel wearied him he came home and waited on her from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 母卒，廬墓不復出。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he built a hut at her tomb and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he lived in a hut by her grave and never left it.

sentences.zh: 漣與縣人杜詔及僧妙复號「三逸」。

translations.literal: Lian, together with Du Zhao of the same county and the monk Miaofu, were called the "Three Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: Lian, Du Zhao of the same county, and the monk Miaofu were known together as the "Three Recluses."

sentences.zh: 薛文，江南和州人。

translations.literal: Xue Wen was a native of Hezhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wen came from Hezhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 弟化禮。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Hua Li.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Hua Li.

sentences.zh: 貧，有母，兄弟一出為傭，一留侍母，迭相代。

translations.literal: Poor, with a mother to support, the brothers took turns — one going out as a hired laborer, one staying to attend her.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor and had a mother to support; one brother would hire out while the other stayed home to care for her, and they alternated.

sentences.zh: 留者在母側絮絮與母語，不使孤坐。

translations.literal: The one who stayed chattered continuously with their mother at her side so that she would not sit alone.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever stayed home kept up a steady stream of talk so their mother would never sit alone.

sentences.zh: 日旰，傭者還，挾酒米魚肉治食奉母，兄弟舞躍歌謳以侑。

translations.literal: At day's end the hired laborer would return, bring wine, rice, fish, and meat, prepare food and serve their mother; the brothers danced, leaped, and sang to entertain her.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the one returning from work would bring wine, rice, fish, and meat, cook a meal for their mother, and both brothers would dance and sing to amuse her.

sentences.zh: 寒，負母曝戶外，兄弟前後為侏儒作態博母笑。

translations.literal: In cold weather they carried their mother outside to sun her; the brothers took turns playing the dwarf and making faces to win their mother's laughter.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they carried their mother outdoors to warm in the sun while the brothers took turns clowning and playing the buffoon to make her laugh.

sentences.zh: 母篤老，病且死，治殯葬畢，毀不能出戶。

translations.literal: Their mother was very old, fell ill and was near death; when the funeral arrangements were complete, grief left them unable to leave the house.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother was very old and gravely ill; after they had seen to her burial, grief confined them within the house.

sentences.zh: 傭主跡至家，文與化禮骨立不能起，哭益哀，數日皆死，時康熙四十二年也。

translations.literal: Their employer traced them to their home; Wen and Hua Li were nothing but bone, unable to rise, weeping more bitterly; within several days both died — this was in the forty-second year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When their employer tracked them down, Wen and Hua Li were wasted to the bone and could not rise, weeping ever more bitterly; within days both died, in the forty-second year of the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 知州何偉表其閭。

translations.literal: Prefect He Wei had their lane officially commended.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect He Wei commended their neighborhood for its example.

sentences.zh: 偉勤於民，卒，民祠焉。

translations.literal: Wei was diligent on behalf of the people; when he died, the people erected a shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: He Wei had been devoted to the people; when he died they built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，學政硃筠令以文、化禮附韋祠。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong era, Educational Commissioner Zhu Yun ordered Wen and Hua Li to be enshrined in the Wei shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong period Educational Commissioner Zhu Yun had Wen and Hua Li added to He's shrine.

sentences.zh: 曹孝童，江南無錫人。

translations.literal: Cao Xiaotong was a native of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiaotong came from Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 居南郭，父為圬者。

translations.literal: He lived in the southern suburbs; his father was a plasterer.
translations.idiomatic: He lived outside the south gate; his father was a house painter.

sentences.zh: 童五歲，父或扃戶出，則竟日不食。

translations.literal: When Xiaotong was five, if his father sometimes locked the door and went out, he would go the whole day without eating.
translations.idiomatic: At five years old, whenever his father locked up and went out Xiaotong would refuse food all day.

sentences.zh: 鄰或哺之，泣不食，俟父歸同食。

translations.literal: Neighbors sometimes fed him; he wept and would not eat, waiting for his father to return and eat together.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors tried to feed him, but he wept and refused to eat until his father came home to share a meal.

sentences.zh: 父死，童嗚咽匍匐死父側，鄰市棺為斂。

translations.literal: When his father died, Xiaotong sobbed and crawled and died at his father's side; neighbors purchased a coffin and laid him out.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died Xiaotong sobbed, crawled to his side, and died there; neighbors bought a coffin for him.

sentences.zh: 丁履豫，江南婁縣人。

translations.literal: Ding Luyu was a native of Lou County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Luyu came from Lou County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was filial in serving his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early and served his mother filially.

sentences.zh: 兄二、弟一皆出遊，以歲所入畀履豫，使營甘旨。

translations.literal: Two elder brothers and one younger brother all traveled away; they gave their yearly earnings to Luyu so he could provide delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: His two older brothers and one younger brother all worked away from home and handed their year's earnings to Luyu to provide their mother with good food.

sentences.zh: 母卒將斂，畫師貌母像絕肖，履豫諦視久之，大慟，僕地遽絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died and was about to be encoffined, a painter's portrait of his mother was lifelike; Luyu gazed at it intently for a long time, then gave a great cry of grief, fell prostrate, and suddenly perished.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and lay ready for burial, a painter's portrait of her was uncannily true; Luyu stared at it a long time, then broke into violent grief, collapsed, and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 鍾保，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhong Bao was a Bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Bao belonged to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父希晉，以步軍校從討吳三桂，積功當遷，鍾保以父老，力勸請休奉養。

translations.literal: His father Xi Jin, an infantry company commander, followed the campaign against Wu Sangui and by accumulated merit was due for promotion; Zhong Bao, because his father was old, strenuously urged him to request retirement to support and nourish him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi Jin, an infantry company commander who had campaigned against Wu Sangui, had earned promotion; Zhong Bao, seeing how old his father was, urged him hard to retire and accept support at home.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，自刑部筆帖式累遷刑部郎中，居父喪哀慟，水漿不入口。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, from a clerk in the Board of Punishments he was promoted step by step to director in that board; in mourning for his father he grieved bitterly and would not take water or food.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he rose from a clerk in the Board of Punishments to a department director; when his father died he mourned so bitterly that he refused even water.

sentences.zh: 事母尤謹，歸必侍母側。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was especially careful; whenever he returned he must attend at her side.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to his mother and always waited on her whenever he came home.

sentences.zh: 兄盪產，撫其孤，祖遺田宅悉推與之。

translations.literal: His elder brother squandered the family property; he raised the brother's orphaned children and gave over to them all the fields and houses inherited from their grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother lost the family fortune he raised the orphans and surrendered to them all the ancestral fields and homestead.

sentences.zh: 弟貧，週之甚力。

translations.literal: His younger brother was poor; he aided him with great effort.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was poor and he supported him generously.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，舉孝子，賜金，旌其門。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he was nominated as a filial son, given gold, and his gate was officially commended.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 he was honored as an exemplary filial son, awarded gold, and his family gate was officially commended.

sentences.zh: 官至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His office reached vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 覺羅色爾岱，滿洲鑲紅旗人，德世庫七世孫也。

translations.literal: Aisin Gioro Seerdai was a Bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Red Banner, seventh-generation descendant of Deshiku.
translations.idiomatic: Aisin Gioro Seerdai belonged to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner and was a seventh-generation descendant of Deshiku.

sentences.zh: 性篤孝。

translations.literal: His nature was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 年十七，父病，醫不效，乃割左臂為糜以進，病稍間，旋歾。

translations.literal: At seventeen his father fell ill; medicine did no good, so he cut flesh from his left arm, made it into a paste, and presented it; the illness eased slightly, but soon afterward his father died.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen his father fell ill beyond cure, so he cut flesh from his left arm and served it as a medicinal paste; the illness briefly eased, but his father soon died.

sentences.zh: 事母益謹，母病飲食減，亦減飲食；

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was even more careful; when his mother's illness reduced her food and drink, he too reduced his food and drink;
translations.idiomatic: He was even more careful with his mother; when illness left her unable to eat properly, he ate less as well;

sentences.zh: 飲食不能進，憂之，亦輟飲食；

translations.literal: when she could not take food or drink, he worried and also stopped food and drink;
translations.idiomatic: when she could not swallow at all he stopped eating too, sick with worry;

sentences.zh: 母能飲食，乃復常。

translations.literal: when his mother could again take food and drink, he then returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: only when she could eat again did he resume his own meals.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命舉忠孝節義，以色爾岱應，詔賜白金，旌其門，授銀庫主事，勤其官，遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an order went out to nominate men of loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness; Seerdai was nominated; the edict awarded white silver, commended his gate, appointed him director of the silver treasury, he was diligent in office, and was promoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 the throne ordered nominations for loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness; Seerdai was chosen, granted silver, and his gate commended; he was appointed to the silver treasury, served diligently, and rose to department director.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，以割臂療親旌者，有翁杜、佟良，與色爾岱同時有克什布。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign those commended for cutting the arm to heal a parent included Weng Du and Tong Liang; contemporaneous with Seerdai was Keshibu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, Weng Du and Tong Liang were among those commended for cutting their arms to heal a parent; Seerdai's contemporary Keshibu did the same.

sentences.zh: 翁杜，滿洲鑲白旗人；

translations.literal: Weng Du was a Bannerman of the Manchu Bordered White Banner;
translations.idiomatic: Weng Du belonged to the Manchu Bordered White Banner;

sentences.zh: 佟良，蒙古鑲黃旗人：官防禦。

translations.literal: Tong Liang was a Bannerman of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner; office: garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Liang belonged to the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner and held the rank of garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 克什布，滿洲鑲紅旗人，官三等侍衛。

translations.literal: Keshibu was a Bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Red Banner; office: third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Keshibu belonged to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner and served as a third-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 王麟瑞，福建南靖人。

translations.literal: Wang Linrui was a native of Nanjing in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Linrui came from Nanjing in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county licentiate.

sentences.zh: 八歲喪母，事後母如所生。

translations.literal: At eight he lost his mother; he treated his stepmother as though she were his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was eight; he served his stepmother with the same devotion he would have given his own.

sentences.zh: 母病暍，非時思食梅，麟瑞繞樹呼號，不食三日，梅夜華，結實奉母，母良愈。

translations.literal: His mother fell ill with heatstroke and at an unseasonable time craved plums; Linrui circled the tree calling and wailing, ate nothing for three days; the plum tree blossomed overnight and bore fruit, which he presented to his mother, and she soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill in the heat and longed for plums out of season, Linrui circled a tree wailing and fasted for three days; overnight it bloomed and bore fruit, which he gave her, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 父喪，廬墓三年，遇虎，虎為卻避。

translations.literal: When his father died he built a hut at the tomb for three years; he encountered a tiger, and the tiger withdrew and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned at the grave for three years; once he met a tiger, and the tiger backed away from him.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，詔舉孝廉方正，縣以麟瑞上。

translations.literal: Early in Yongzheng an edict ordered nomination of filial and upright scholars; the county submitted Linrui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng the throne ordered nominations for filial and upright scholars, and the county put forward Linrui.

sentences.zh: 四年，授陝西道監察御史，出為直隸永平知府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed investigating censor for the Shaanxi circuit and later became prefect of Yongping in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was named an investigating censor on the Shaanxi circuit, then went out to serve as prefect of Yongping in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 李盛山，福建羅源人。

translations.literal: Li Shengshan was a native of Luoyuan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengshan came from Luoyuan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 母病，割肝以救，傷重，卒。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill he cut out his liver to save her; the wound was severe and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he cut out part of his liver to save her; the injury was grave and he died.

sentences.zh: 巡撫常賚疏請旌，下禮部，禮部議輕生愚孝，無旌表之例。

translations.literal: Governor Chang Gai memorialized requesting commendation; the matter was sent to the Board of Rites, which considered it foolish filial piety that threw away life and found no precedent for commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chang Gai petitioned for an official commendation; the Board of Rites ruled it reckless, self-destructive piety and denied any precedent for honoring it.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年三月壬子，世宗諭曰：「朕惟世祖、聖祖臨御萬方，立教明倫，與人為善。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the third month of the sixth year of Yongzheng, the Shizong instructed: "I consider that the Shizu and Shengzu ruled the myriad regions, established teaching and clarified human relations, and practiced benevolence toward men.
translations.idiomatic: On a day in the third month of Yongzheng 6, the Yongzheng Emperor directed: "The Shunzhi and Kangxi emperors governed the realm, set forth moral teaching, clarified the human bonds, and sought the good of their people.

sentences.zh: 而於例慎予旌表者，誠天地好生之盛心，聖人覺世之至道，視人命為至重，不可以愚昧誤戕；

translations.literal: Yet in regulation they were cautious about granting commendation — truly the great heart of Heaven and Earth that cherishes life, the supreme Way of the sage who awakens the age, viewing human life as paramount, not to be mistakenly destroyed through folly;
translations.idiomatic: In awarding official commendations they were deliberately cautious — a reflection of Heaven and Earth's love of life and the sage's duty to awaken the world. Human life is paramount and must not be foolishly thrown away;

sentences.zh: 念孝道為至弘，不可以毀傷為正。

translations.literal: Considering filial piety the utmost greatness, it cannot be made correct through mutilation and injury.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is the greatest of virtues, but it cannot be proved by self-mutilation.

sentences.zh: 但有司未嘗以聖賢經常之道，與國家愛養之心，明白宣示，是以愚夫愚婦救親而捐軀，殉夫而殞命，往往有之。

translations.literal: Yet local officials never clearly proclaimed the constant Way of sages and worthies together with the state's heart of cherishing and nurturing, so foolish men and foolish women who sacrificed themselves to save a parent, or died following a husband, were often found.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials never made plain the regular teaching of the sages together with the state's own care for its people, so simple men and women who died saving a parent or following a husband in death were all too common.

sentences.zh: 既有其事，若不予以旌表，無以彰其苦志。

translations.literal: Once such acts occurred, if commendation were not granted there would be no means to make manifest their bitter determination.
translations.idiomatic: When such acts occurred, withholding commendation would leave their anguished devotion unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 故數十年來雖未定例，仍許奏聞，且有邀恩於常格之外者。

translations.literal: Therefore for several decades although no fixed regulation was established, memorials were still permitted, and some received grace beyond ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For decades, though no fixed rule existed, such cases could still be reported, and some received honors beyond ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 聖祖哀矜下民之盛心，如是其周詳而委曲也。

translations.literal: The Shengzu's great heart of pity and compassion for the common people was thus thorough and comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor's compassion for the common people was as thorough as it was tender.

sentences.zh: 父母愛子，無所不至，若因己病而致其子割肝刲股以充飲饌、和湯藥，縱其子無恙，父母未有不驚憂惻怛慘惕而不安者，況因此而傷生，豈父母所忍聞乎？

translations.literal: Parents love their children without limit; if because of one's own illness one's child cuts out liver or flesh from the thigh to fill food and drink or mix into broth and medicine — even if the child suffers no harm, what parent would not be startled, worried, pained, frightened, and ill at ease? How much less if life is injured thereby — how could parents bear to hear of it?
translations.idiomatic: Parents love their children without limit. If a parent's illness drove a son to cut out his liver or flesh from his thigh for food or medicine, even when the child survived no parent could fail to be shocked and stricken with dread — how much less when the attempt cost a life? What parent could bear to hear of that?

sentences.zh: 父母有疾，固人子盡心竭力之時，儻能至誠純孝，必且感天地、動鬼神，不必以驚世駭俗之為，著奇於日用倫常之外。

translations.literal: When parents are ill, it is naturally the time for a child to exhaust heart and strength; if one can be utterly sincere in pure filial piety, surely Heaven and Earth will be moved and ghosts and spirits stirred — there is no need for acts that startle the world and shock custom, making a spectacle beyond daily human relations.
translations.idiomatic: When parents fall ill, a child should give all his heart and strength; sincere filial piety can move Heaven and touch the spirits. There is no need for sensational acts that go beyond ordinary family duty.

sentences.zh: 婦人從一之義，醮而不改，乃天下之正道，然烈婦難，節婦尤難。

translations.literal: The principle for a woman of following one man — remarriage without change — is the correct Way under Heaven; yet a fierce chaste woman is difficult, a chaste widow is even more difficult.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's duty to keep faith with one husband and never remarry is the right path under Heaven — yet martyrdom for chastity is rare, and lifelong widowhood rarer still.

sentences.zh: 夫亡之後，婦職之當盡者更多，上有翁姑，則當代為奉養。

translations.literal: After a husband's death, there is more a wife's duty should fulfill; if there are parents-in-law above, she should support and nourish them in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: After a husband dies a widow's duties multiply; if parents-in-law survive, she must support them in his place.

sentences.zh: 他如修治蘋蘩，經理家業，其事難以悉數，安得以一死畢其責乎？

translations.literal: Other matters such as tending ceremonial herbs, managing household affairs — these tasks are too many to count in full; how could one discharge one's responsibility with death alone?
translations.idiomatic: She must maintain the household altar, manage the family estate, and much else besides — duties too numerous to list. How can she fulfill them all by dying?

sentences.zh: 朕今特頒訓諭，有司廣為宣示，俾知孝子節婦，自有常經，倫常之地，皆合中庸，以毋負國家教養矜全之德。
