translations.literal: I now specially issue this instruction; let officials proclaim it widely, so that filial sons and chaste women know there is a constant standard, and in the realm of human relations all should conform to the mean, so as not to betray the state's virtue of nurturing, cherishing, and preserving life.
translations.idiomatic: I now issue this instruction for officials to proclaim far and wide, so that filial sons and chaste widows understand the proper standard — that human bonds should follow the middle way and honor the state's care in nurturing and preserving life.

sentences.zh: 倘訓諭之後，仍有不愛軀命，蹈於危亡者，朕亦不概加旌表，以成激烈輕生之習也。

translations.literal: If after this instruction there are still those who do not cherish life and rush toward danger and death, I likewise will not broadly grant commendation, so as not to foster the custom of fierce disregard for life.
translations.idiomatic: If after this instruction anyone still recklessly courts death, I will no longer grant commendation across the board, lest we encourage a fashion for rash self-destruction.

sentences.zh: 」盛山仍予旌表。

translations.literal: " Shengshan was still granted commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Shengshan was still honored.

sentences.zh: 李悃，河南開封府人，失其縣。

translations.literal: Li Kun was from Kaifeng Prefecture in Henan; his county is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kun came from Kaifeng Prefecture in Henan; his home county is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 貧為木工，父病痺，奉侍惟謹。

translations.literal: Poor, he worked as a carpenter; his father suffered paralysis and he served and attended him with sole care.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and working as a carpenter, he nursed his paralyzed father with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 歲歉，不能養，乃行乞於市，歸啖父。

translations.literal: In a bad harvest year he could not support him, so he begged in the market and returned to feed his father.
translations.idiomatic: When famine made support impossible he begged in the streets and fed what he got to his father.

sentences.zh: 後得賑穀一石，慮不能繼，日舂升許供父，而以秕自咽。

translations.literal: Later he received one shi of relief grain; fearing it would not last, each day he husked about a sheng for his father while he swallowed the chaff himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received a shi of relief grain; afraid it would not last, he husked a little each day for his father and ate the chaff himself.

sentences.zh: 父病劇，夜中鄰人時聞悃撫摩嗟泣聲，遲明則悃抱父足死矣，父亦一慟而絕。

translations.literal: When his father's illness grew severe, at night neighbors sometimes heard Kun's sounds of stroking, sighing, and weeping; at dawn Kun was found embracing his father's feet, dead; his father also, with one cry of grief, expired.
translations.idiomatic: As his father worsened, neighbors heard Kun through the night stroking and sighing over him; at dawn Kun was found dead with his arms around his father's feet, and his father died in a single burst of grief.

sentences.zh: 鄰人愍其孝，收而葬之。

translations.literal: Neighbors pitied his filial piety and gathered and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his devotion, neighbors laid them out and buried them together.

sentences.zh: 奚緝營，字聖輝，江蘇寶山人。

translations.literal: Xi Jiying, courtesy name Shenghui, was a native of Baoshan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jiying, styled Shenghui, came from Baoshan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父士本，以孝旌。

translations.literal: His father Shiben was commended for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shiben had been honored for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 緝營幼讀論語，至「父母之年，不可不知」，輒隕涕簌簌，師奇之，謂真孝子子也。

translations.literal: When Jiying as a child read the Analects and came to "The years of one's parents must not be unknown," he would shed tears in streams; his teacher marvelled and said he was truly a filial son's son.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy reading the Analects, he wept whenever he reached "A son must know the years of his parents"; his teacher marvelled and called him a born filial son.

sentences.zh: 母病，刲臂以療。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill he cut flesh from his arm to heal her.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he cut flesh from his arm to heal her.

sentences.zh: 士本老，惡寒，緝營夜抱父足眠，以為常。

translations.literal: Shiben was old and hated the cold; Jiying at night held his father's feet while sleeping — this became his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Shiben was old and felt the cold keenly; Jiying made it his habit to sleep holding his father's feet at night.

sentences.zh: 兩弟早卒，撫其孤如所生。

translations.literal: Two younger brothers died early; he raised their orphans as though they were his own children.
translations.idiomatic: When two younger brothers died young he raised their orphans as his own.

sentences.zh: 女兄嫁而貧，從妹寡，皆依以居，為營婚嫁。

translations.literal: An elder sister married into poverty; a younger cousin was widowed; all relied on him for residence, and he arranged marriages for them.
translations.idiomatic: An older sister married into poverty and a younger cousin was widowed; both lived with him and he saw to their marriages.

sentences.zh: 周士晉，江蘇嘉定人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shijin was a native of Jiading in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shijin came from Jiading in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 母病久，醫言惟飲人乳可生，士晉子生方九月，謀於妻李，棄道旁，以乳乳母。

translations.literal: His mother's illness was long; doctors said only drinking human milk could save her; Shijin's son had been born only nine months before; he consulted with his wife Li, and they abandoned the child by the roadside so her milk could nourish his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been ill a long time; doctors said only human milk could save her. Shijin's son was only nine months old; he and his wife Li agreed to abandon the boy by the roadside so she could nurse his mother.

sentences.zh: 母病已，問兒，以殤對，後李不復姙，亦無怨。

translations.literal: When his mother's illness was cured she asked about the child; he answered that the infant had died; later Li never conceived again, yet bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother recovered she asked after the child; he said the boy had died in infancy. Li never bore another child, yet never complained.

sentences.zh: 越十二年，有僧為殷氏子推命，年月日與士晉兒同，詰之，則得諸道旁者也，父子得復合。

translations.literal: Twelve years later a monk cast the horoscope for a son of the Yin clan; the year, month, and day matched Shijin's son; on questioning, it turned out he had been picked up from the roadside; father and son were reunited.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later a monk reading the horoscope of a Yin family boy found his birth date identical to Shijin's lost son; inquiry showed he had been found by the roadside, and father and son were reunited.

sentences.zh: 黃有則，湖南邵陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Youze was a native of Shaoyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Youze came from Shaoyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 四歲喪父，母孫劬苦育以長。

translations.literal: At four he lost his father; his mother Sun raised him through bitter toil.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was four; his mother Sun raised him through hard labor.

sentences.zh: 遣就傅，或迂之，孫曰：「吾忍死，不欲兒廢學也。

translations.literal: She sent him to a tutor; when someone tried to dissuade her, Sun said, "I endure death because I do not want my son to abandon his studies.
translations.idiomatic: She sent him to school; when someone suggested the trip was too far, Sun said, "I will endure whatever hardship it takes — I will not let my son leave off his studies.

sentences.zh: 」有則大感慟，奮學，客授養母。

translations.literal: " Youze was greatly moved and grieved, applied himself to study, and supported his mother by teaching as a hired tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into his books and supported his mother by tutoring abroad.

sentences.zh: 夏無帳，主人以進，命撤之，曰：「吾母無此也。

translations.literal: In summer without a mosquito net, his employer offered one; he ordered it removed and said, "My mother has not this.
translations.idiomatic: One summer he had no mosquito net; when his employer offered one he refused, saying, "My mother has none.

sentences.zh: 」寒為製棉衣，又卻之，曰：「家貧，無以暖母，不忍享奇溫。

translations.literal: " In cold weather a padded jacket was made for him; he again refused it and said, "The family is poor and has no means to warm Mother; I cannot bear to enjoy exceptional warmth.
translations.idiomatic: In winter his employer made him a padded coat, but he refused again: "We are too poor to keep my mother warm — I cannot enjoy comfort she lacks.

sentences.zh: 」一夕風雪，既寐，復起，行三十里歸省母。

translations.literal: " One night in wind and snow, after he had fallen asleep he rose again and walked thirty li to return and visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: One snowy night he woke from sleep and walked thirty li home to see his mother.

sentences.zh: 母喜曰：「吾正思兒。

translations.literal: His mother said with joy, "I was just thinking of my son.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said happily, "I was just thinking of you.

sentences.zh: 」是時母逾九十，有則亦六十矣。

translations.literal: " At that time his mother was over ninety, and Youze was also sixty.
translations.idiomatic: By then his mother was over ninety and Youze himself was sixty.

sentences.zh: 母喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died he died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he succumbed to grief.

sentences.zh: 王尚毅，陝西郃陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Shangyi was a native of Heyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shangyi came from Heyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 為人傭。

translations.literal: He worked as a hired laborer for others.
translations.idiomatic: He hired out his labor to others.

sentences.zh: 母佞佛，欲鑿山造佛像，力不逮，將死，以命尚毅。

translations.literal: His mother was devoted to Buddhism and wished to carve a mountain to make Buddhist images; her strength did not suffice; as she was about to die she charged Shangyi with the task.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was devoted to Buddhism and wished to carve Buddha images from a mountainside, but lacked the strength; on her deathbed she charged Shangyi with fulfilling her wish.

sentences.zh: 尚毅傭，嗇衣食積錢，買山闢洞，琢石為佛像，洞六，像十二，皆手造。

translations.literal: Shangyi hired out his labor, scrimped on food and clothing to save money, bought a mountain and opened caves, carved stone into Buddhist images — six caves, twelve images, all made by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyi hired himself out, scrimped on food and clothing to save money, bought a hillside and carved six caves with twelve stone Buddha images, every one fashioned by his own hand.

sentences.zh: 或愍而助之，謝曰：「力不己出，非敬母命也。

translations.literal: When someone pitied him and offered help, he declined and said, "If the labor is not my own, it is not honoring Mother's command."
translations.idiomatic: When others offered to help out of pity he refused, saying, "If the work is not mine alone, I am not fulfilling my mother's charge."

sentences.zh: 」錢盡乃輟，復出傭，得錢更為之，如是三十餘年。

translations.literal: " When his money was exhausted he would stop, go out again as a hired laborer, earn money and resume the work — thus for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: When his money ran out he stopped, hired out again, and resumed work once he had saved enough — for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 山植柏，圍以紫荊，洞上下蒔迎春，洞成方冬，花盡開，山人怪之，名曰九華洞。

translations.literal: On the mountain he planted cypress, surrounded it with bauhinia, and above and below the caves planted winter jasmine; when the caves were completed it was just winter, yet the flowers all bloomed; mountain people marvelled and named it Jiuhua Cave.
translations.idiomatic: He planted cypress on the mountain, ringed it with bauhinia, and set winter jasmine around the caves; when the work was done it was midwinter, yet every blossom opened — the local people marvelled and named it the Jiuhua Cave.

sentences.zh: 山無水，鑿池而雨至，遂不涸，名曰青龍池。

translations.literal: The mountain had no water; he carved a pool and when rain came it never dried up; it was named Qinglong Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain had no spring, so he dug a pool that filled with rain and never ran dry; they called it the Azure Dragon Pool.

sentences.zh: 胡锳，浙江上虞人。

translations.literal: Hu Ying was a native of Shangyu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying came from Shangyu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 锳九歲從母汲，母墮井，锳呼救未至，亦躍入井，救至，引以出，俱不死。

translations.literal: At nine Ying followed his mother to draw water; she fell into a well; Ying called for help but before rescue arrived he also leaped into the well; when help came they were pulled out, and both survived.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he went with his mother to draw water; when she fell into a well he shouted for help, then jumped in after her before rescuers arrived; both were pulled out alive.

sentences.zh: 中歲遊陝西，一夕忽心痛，曰：「殆吾父病耶？

translations.literal: In midlife he traveled in Shaanxi; one night he suddenly felt heart pain and said, "Could my father be ill?"
translations.idiomatic: In middle age he was traveling in Shaanxi when one night his heart seized with pain; he said, "Could my father be ill?"

sentences.zh: 」馳還，父正病，旋卒，哀慟盡禮。

translations.literal: " He raced back; his father was indeed ill and soon died; he grieved and observed every rite of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He raced home and found his father gravely ill; his father soon died, and he mourned with full ritual observance.

sentences.zh: 方冬母病，求醫，途遇盜，衣盡褫，冒寒行數十里，與醫俱歸。

translations.literal: In winter his mother fell ill; he went to seek a doctor, met bandits on the road who stripped him of all his clothes; braving the cold he walked scores of li and returned home with the doctor.
translations.idiomatic: One winter his mother fell ill; on the road to fetch a doctor he was robbed of every garment, yet he walked dozens of li through the cold and brought the physician home.

sentences.zh: 李三，江蘇宜興人。

translations.literal: Li San was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Li San came from Yixing in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 一目眇，一足跛。

translations.literal: One eye was blind, one leg was lame.
translations.idiomatic: He was blind in one eye and lame in one leg.

sentences.zh: 父死，二兄皆娶，析產，有田六畝、屋四椽、舟一，二兄分田、屋，而畀三以舟。

translations.literal: When his father died both elder brothers had married and they divided the property: six mu of fields, a four-bay house, and one boat; the elder brothers took the fields and house and gave San the boat.
translations.idiomatic: After their father died the two older brothers married and split the estate — six mu of land, a four-bay house, and one boat; the brothers took the land and house and left San the boat.

sentences.zh: 迭養母，三奉母食必有肉，母至二兄所，三輒私致甘旨。

translations.literal: They took turns supporting their mother; when San served her food there was always meat; when she went to the elder brothers' homes San would secretly send delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: They took turns caring for their mother; San always put meat in her meals, and when she stayed with his brothers he secretly sent delicacies as well.

sentences.zh: 二兄死，嫂一前死、一嫁，三獨奉母。

translations.literal: When both elder brothers died — one sister-in-law had died earlier, the other remarried — San alone supported their mother.
translations.idiomatic: When both brothers died — one sister-in-law had already passed, the other remarried — San alone cared for their mother.

sentences.zh: 晨爨畢，乃以舟應客，或當出五十里外，度盡日不能返，雖重僱不之許。

translations.literal: After finishing the morning cooking he would take the boat for passengers; if a job would take him fifty li or more and he judged he could not return the same day, even for high pay he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After cooking her morning meal he would ferry passengers; if a job would take him more than fifty li and keep him away all day, he refused even the highest pay.

sentences.zh: 事母三十年，鄰里稱其孝，撫兄子慈，而教之嚴。

translations.literal: He served his mother for thirty years; neighbors praised his filial piety; he was kind in raising his brothers' sons but strict in teaching them.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his mother thirty years, and neighbors praised his devotion; he raised his brothers' sons with kindness but taught them strictly.

sentences.zh: 母將死，呼孫執手泣曰：「兒學好，毋累汝叔怒！

translations.literal: As their mother was about to die she called her grandson, took his hand, and wept, saying, "Study well, do not make your uncle angry!"
translations.idiomatic: As she lay dying she called her grandson, took his hand, and wept: "Study hard — do not anger your uncle!"

sentences.zh: 」自是不復怒其兄子。

translations.literal: " From that time he no longer grew angry with his brothers' sons.
translations.idiomatic: After that he never again lost his temper with his brothers' sons.

sentences.zh: 張夢維，直隸元城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mengwei was a native of Yuancheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mengwei came from Yuancheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 縣諸生。

translations.literal: A county licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county licentiate.

sentences.zh: 父晚病風痺，夢維日侍左右，臥起飲食溲溺皆躬自扶持。

translations.literal: His father in his later years suffered from wind paralysis; Mengwei attended him day by day at his side; lying down, rising, eating, drinking, urinating, and defecating — all he personally supported.
translations.idiomatic: In his father's later years wind paralysis crippled him; Mengwei waited on him daily, helping him in every movement, meal, and bodily need.

sentences.zh: 父愍其勞，呵之去，少退，复前，數年不少懈。

translations.literal: His father pitied his labors and scolded him to leave; he would retreat a little then come forward again — for several years he never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: His father, pitying his exhaustion, ordered him away; he would step back briefly, then return — and never slackened for years.

sentences.zh: 事母如事父。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was as in serving his father.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother with the same devotion he had shown his father.

sentences.zh: 居喪哀毀，準家禮，屏俗習。

translations.literal: In mourning he grieved so bitterly his health failed; he followed the family rites and shunned vulgar customs.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he grieved until his health broke; he followed the family rites and rejected vulgar custom.

sentences.zh: 弟病疽，為剪髮灼艾，日數省視，及卒，慟甚，幾喪明。

translations.literal: His younger brother had carbuncle disease; he cut his hair and applied moxa for him, visited several times daily, and when he died grieved so bitterly he nearly lost his sight.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother fell ill with a festering sore he cut his hair and burned moxa for him, visiting several times a day; when his brother died his grief nearly cost him his sight.

sentences.zh: 弟妻或詬誶，待之有加，撫孤女逾己出，弟妻卒悟且悔。

translations.literal: His brother's wife sometimes scolded and reviled him; he treated her all the more kindly, raised the orphaned daughter better than his own, until the brother's wife finally understood and repented.
translations.idiomatic: Though his sister-in-law sometimes abused him, he treated her only more kindly and raised the orphaned girl as tenderly as his own; in time she understood and repented.

sentences.zh: 少師郡人衛鶴鳴，治程、硃之學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Wei Heming of the same prefecture, who specialized in the Cheng-Zhu school of Neo-Confucianism.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under his countyman Wei Heming, a scholar of the Cheng-Zhu Neo-Confucian tradition.

sentences.zh: 鶴鳴卒，心喪三年。

translations.literal: When Heming died, he observed heart-mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Heming died he observed three years of informal mourning from the heart.

sentences.zh: 授弟子孝經、小學，以力行為本。

translations.literal: He taught his pupils the Classic of Filial Piety and the Xiaoxue, taking earnest practice as fundamental.
translations.idiomatic: He taught students from the Classic of Filial Piety and the Xiaoxue, with earnest practice at the core.

sentences.zh: 樂太希，湖北通山縣人。

translations.literal: Yue Taixi was a native of Tongshan County in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Taixi came from Tongshan County in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 幼慧，三歲母負以嬉，墮地傷額。

translations.literal: Clever as a child, at three his mother carried him on her back to play and he fell to the ground, injuring his forehead.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever as a child; at three his mother was playing with him on her back when he fell and injured his forehead.

sentences.zh: 祖母問，詭對，恐祖母見憐而怒母也。

translations.literal: When his grandmother asked, he answered evasively, fearing that if his grandmother showed pity she would be angry with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother asked what happened he lied, fearing pity for him would turn her anger on his mother.

sentences.zh: 父疾，抑搔澣濯，晝夜不去側。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill he rubbed, scratched, washed, and bathed him, never leaving his side day or night.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill he washed and tended him without leaving his side day or night.

sentences.zh: 居喪盡哀，既葬，恆繞墓悲痛。

translations.literal: In mourning he grieved to the utmost; after burial he constantly circled the tomb in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned with full grief; after burial he constantly walked the grave in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 母疾及喪亦如之，廬墓側居五年。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill and in mourning he did likewise, living in a hut beside the tomb for five years.
translations.idiomatic: He did the same when his mother fell ill and died, living in a hut beside her grave for five years.

sentences.zh: 早為諸生，以事親不應試，或延使授經，輒辭，慮違親也。

translations.literal: Early he became a licentiate, but to serve his parents he did not sit for examinations; when invited to teach the classics he always declined, fearing to neglect his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Though he became a licentiate early, he skipped examinations to care for his parents; when invited to teach he always refused, unwilling to neglect them.

sentences.zh: 親既終，益篤學。

translations.literal: After his parents had both died he applied himself all the more to study.
translations.idiomatic: After both parents had died he devoted himself more deeply to his studies.

sentences.zh: 董盛祖，雲南黑鹽井人。

translations.literal: Dong Shengzhu was a native of Heiyanjing in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shengzhu came from Heiyanjing in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 盛祖不知書，早失父，事母謹，起居飲食侍視不少懈。

translations.literal: Shengzhu could not read; he lost his father early; in serving his mother he was careful — attending and watching over her rising, sleeping, eating, and drinking without the slightest slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate and fatherless from early on, he cared for his mother meticulously, never slackening in attending her daily needs.

sentences.zh: 一妹嫁里中，盛祖出負販，呼妹還侍母，妹亦善事母如盛祖。

translations.literal: One younger sister married within the village; when Shengzhu went out peddling he called his sister back to attend their mother; the sister also served their mother well like Shengzhu.
translations.idiomatic: When a younger sister married locally he would call her home whenever he went peddling so she could care for their mother, and she served their mother as devotedly as he did.

sentences.zh: 盛祖行遇蛇當道，驚曰：「母得無病乎？

translations.literal: As Shengzhu was traveling he met a snake blocking the road and said in alarm, "Could Mother be ill?"
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met a snake blocking his path and cried out in alarm, "Could my mother be ill?"

sentences.zh: 」歸則母方病，呼祖，人皆怪之。

translations.literal: " When he returned his mother had just fallen ill, calling for Shengzhu; everyone marvelled at it.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed home and found his mother just fallen ill, calling for him — everyone found it uncanny.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哭甚哀，或慟絕，鄰里驚救之，乃甦。

translations.literal: At his mother's funeral he wept with great grief, sometimes falling unconscious; neighbors rushed to revive him.
translations.idiomatic: At her funeral he wept until he lost consciousness; neighbors rushed to revive him.

sentences.zh: 盛祖有妻早亡，不更娶。

translations.literal: Shengzhu had a wife who died early; he never remarried.
translations.idiomatic: His wife had died young and he never remarried.

sentences.zh: 或勸之，曰：「娶婦以事親，顧賢者實難。

translations.literal: When someone urged him he said, "One takes a wife to serve one's parents, but a worthy one is truly hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: When urged to remarry he said, "A man marries to serve his parents — but a worthy wife is hard to find.

sentences.zh: 脫不賢，將戾吾母，吾能安乎？

translations.literal: If she were unworthy she would wrong my mother — how could I be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: If she were unworthy she would grieve my mother — how could I rest easy?"

sentences.zh: 」卒不娶。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not marry.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never married.

sentences.zh: 未終喪，遂卒。

translations.literal: Before mourning was complete he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 徐守仁，安徽青陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Shouren was a native of Qingyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shouren came from Qingyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 世為農，未嘗讀書。

translations.literal: His family for generations were farmers; he had never studied books.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations and he had never learned to read.

sentences.zh: 四歲而孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned at four, he was filial in serving his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at four, he served his mother filially.

sentences.zh: 得傭直，市酒肉奉母，母呼共食，輒以持齋謝，實不忍分甘也。

translations.literal: When he earned wages from hired labor he bought wine and meat to serve his mother; when she called him to eat together he would decline on the pretext of fasting — in truth he could not bear to share the delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his wages on wine and meat for his mother; when she invited him to share a meal he pleaded fasting — he could not bear to partake while she had so little.

sentences.zh: 母歿，哀慟。

translations.literal: When his mother died he grieved bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he grieved bitterly.

sentences.zh: 既葬，露處墓側，蛇虺不避，里人哀之，為廬舍飲食焉。

translations.literal: After burial he slept exposed beside the tomb, not avoiding snakes; villagers pitied him and built a hut with food and drink for him.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he slept in the open beside the grave, unafraid of snakes; neighbors pitied him and built a hut where he could eat and sleep.

sentences.zh: 守仁並奉其父木主以居，四年，乃還其室，鬚髮皆白。

translations.literal: Shouren also kept his father's spirit tablet and dwelled with it; after four years he returned to his house, his beard and hair all white.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his father's spirit tablet there as well; after four years he went home with his hair and beard turned white.

sentences.zh: 李鳳翔，直隸武強人。

translations.literal: Li Fengxiang was a native of Wuqiang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengxiang came from Wuqiang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 善事父母。

translations.literal: He was good at serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his parents.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔以父老，自請佐家事，而督諸弟讀書、習射，應文、武試。

translations.literal: Because his father was old Fengxiang volunteered to manage household affairs while supervising his younger brothers in reading, archery practice, and sitting for civil and military examinations.
translations.idiomatic: As his father aged Fengxiang took charge of the household and saw to his younger brothers' studies, archery, and civil and military examinations.

sentences.zh: 父將終，遺命析產，心憐幼子而未有言。

translations.literal: As his father was about to die he left instructions to divide the property; in his heart he pitied the youngest son but said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed his father ordered the estate divided but silently pitied his youngest son.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔察父意，益以所分三之一。

translations.literal: Fengxiang perceived his father's intent and added a third of his own share to the youngest brother's portion.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his father's unspoken wish, Fengxiang gave the youngest brother an extra third of his own share.

sentences.zh: 父歾，事母益謹。

translations.literal: When his father died he was even more careful in serving his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died he was even more devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 道光初，滹沱連歲氾溢，閭里盪析，負鳳翔債者二千餘緡，悉焚其券，复散錢濟貧者。

translations.literal: Early in the Daoguang reign the Hutuo River flooded year after year; villages were washed away; those who owed Fengxiang more than two thousand strings of cash — he burned all their bonds and also distributed money to aid the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In early Daoguang the Hutuo flooded year after year, villages washed away; Fengxiang burned bonds for more than two thousand strings of cash owed him and gave money to the poor.

sentences.zh: 又遇旱，所藝蔬果任飢者採食。

translations.literal: When drought came again he allowed the hungry to pick and eat the vegetables and fruits he cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he let the hungry take whatever they needed from his vegetable garden.

sentences.zh: 族子早孤，他縣人以迎喪遇盜，皆厚週之。

translations.literal: A clansman's son was orphaned early; when people of other counties came to fetch a coffin and met with bandits, he generously aided them all.
translations.idiomatic: He generously helped an orphaned clansman's son and others from neighboring counties who lost everything to bandits while transporting coffins.

sentences.zh: 或將屠馬，鳳翔贖以歸，馬馴異常畜，鄉人感之，遂無屠馬者。

translations.literal: When someone was about to slaughter a horse Fengxiang redeemed it and brought it home; the horse was unusually tame; villagers were moved and thereafter no one slaughtered horses.
translations.idiomatic: When someone was about to slaughter a horse he bought it back; the horse proved unusually gentle, the village was moved, and no one there slaughtered horses again.

sentences.zh: 卯觀成，雲南恩安人。

translations.literal: Mao Guancheng was a native of En'an in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Guancheng came from En'an in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 父漢而母夷。

translations.literal: His father was Han Chinese and his mother was an ethnic minority woman.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Han Chinese and his mother belonged to a local minority people.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙亂，父死，母被掠，鬻為婢。

translations.literal: During the Wumeng rebellion his father died and his mother was captured and sold as a maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wumeng rebellion his father died and raiders seized his mother and sold her into servitude.

sentences.zh: 亂定，觀成無所依，為昭通禁卒。

translations.literal: When the rebellion ended Guancheng had nowhere to depend on and became a prison guard at Zhaotong.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion ended he was left alone and became a prison guard at Zhaotong.

sentences.zh: 父母嘗為聘婦，舅促觀成娶，娶而不與婚。

translations.literal: His parents had once arranged a betrothal for him; his uncle urged Guancheng to marry, so he married but did not consummate the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His parents had betrothed him; his uncle pressed him to marry, so he wed but never consummated the marriage.

sentences.zh: 三年，舅詰之，曰：「吾非不欲婚也，行將嫁吾未婚之妻，取所直歸吾母。

translations.literal: After three years his uncle questioned him; he said, "It is not that I do not wish to marry; I mean to marry off my unmarried wife, take the bride-price, and return with it to redeem my mother.
translations.idiomatic: After three years his uncle pressed him; he said, "I do want to marry — but I plan to marry off my bride, take her bride-price, and use it to redeem my mother.

sentences.zh: 與之婚，情不能割，義亦不可出也。

translations.literal: If I consummated the marriage I could not sever the bond of feeling, nor could I in propriety send her away."
translations.idiomatic: If I slept with her I could not bear to part from her — yet decency forbade casting her aside."

sentences.zh: 」語且泣。

translations.literal: " As he spoke he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He said this through tears.

sentences.zh: 有義之者，募得六十金，以半贖其母，半為營廬舍，成婚，仍為禁卒以養母。

translations.literal: Someone moved by righteousness collected sixty taels of silver; half redeemed his mother, half built a dwelling; the marriage was consummated, and he continued as a prison guard to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his plight, others raised sixty taels — half to redeem his mother, half for a home; he consummated his marriage and kept guard duty to support her.

sentences.zh: 葛大賓，字興森，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Ge Dabin, courtesy name Xingsen, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Dabin, styled Xingsen, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 四歲喪父，哀慟如成人。

translations.literal: At four he lost his father and grieved like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was four, and he mourned like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 喪終，值忌日，出主祭，主僕，粉落「葛」字脫，露「週」姓，蓋木工飾周氏廢主為之。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, on a death anniversary he brought out the spirit tablet for sacrifice; the tablet was old, the plaster fell away, the character "Ge" peeled off and the surname "Zhou" was revealed — a carpenter had made it from a discarded Zhou-family tablet and refinished it.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning, on a death anniversary he brought out the spirit tablet for sacrifice; the plaster crumbled, the character "Ge" fell away, and the surname "Zhou" showed through — a carpenter had refinished an old Zhou-family tablet.

sentences.zh: 大賓痛哭引咎，告墓易主。

translations.literal: Dabin wept bitterly, accepted blame, told his father at the grave, and replaced the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Dabin wept, blamed himself, told his father at the grave, and replaced the tablet.

sentences.zh: 事母鉅細必躬，疾嘗藥，生徒有餽則獻。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he personally attended to every detail great and small; when she was ill he tasted her medicine; when students brought gifts he presented them to her.
translations.idiomatic: He personally tended his mother in every detail; when she was ill he tasted her medicine first, and gifts from his students went straight to her.

sentences.zh: 嘗出客授，獨坐心動，亟還呼母，母出，屋後山遽頹，壓母坐處。

translations.literal: Once while teaching away from home he was sitting alone when his heart stirred; he hurried back and called his mother out; as she emerged the mountain behind the house suddenly collapsed, crushing the spot where she had been sitting.
translations.idiomatic: While teaching abroad he felt a sudden unease, rushed home, and called his mother out just as the hillside behind the house collapsed onto the spot where she had been sitting.

sentences.zh: 母歿，飲不入口者五日。

translations.literal: When his mother died he took no food or drink for five days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he refused all food and drink for five days.

sentences.zh: 既葬，不脫衰，腰以下縷皆盡。

translations.literal: After burial he did not remove his mourning garments; the hemp threads below the waist were entirely worn through.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he never removed his mourning clothes; the hemp filaments below his waist wore through entirely.

sentences.zh: 喪終，祭必哀，兄弟既分居，財盡，大賓復與同居，通財無所私。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he always wept at sacrifice; his brothers had already divided households and exhausted their wealth; Dabin lived together with them again, sharing property without private reserve.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he wept at every sacrifice; though his brothers had separated and lost their fortunes, he moved back in with them and shared everything without keeping anything for himself.

sentences.zh: 歿則庀其喪，無子，為立後。

translations.literal: When they died he arranged their funerals; those without sons — he established heirs for them.
translations.idiomatic: When they died he arranged their funerals; for those without sons he established heirs.

sentences.zh: 呂斅孚，湖南永定人。

translations.literal: Lu Xiaofu was a native of Yongding in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiaofu came from Yongding in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父孟卿，貧，以客授自給。

translations.literal: His father Mengqing was poor and supported himself by teaching as a hired tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengqing was poor and made a living tutoring abroad.

sentences.zh: 母病將殆，思肉食，斅孚方七歲，貸諸屠，屠不可，泣而歸。

translations.literal: His mother was gravely ill and craved meat; Xiaofu was just seven; he begged credit from the butcher, who refused; he wept and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother lay gravely ill and craved meat, seven-year-old Xiaofu begged the butcher on credit, was refused, and came home weeping.

sentences.zh: 聞母呻吟，益痛，內念股肉可啗母，取廚刀礪使利，割右股四寸許，授其女弟，方五歲，令就爐火炙以進。

translations.literal: Hearing his mother groan he grieved more bitterly; inwardly he thought flesh from his thigh could feed her; he took a kitchen knife, sharpened it, cut about four inches from his right thigh, gave it to his younger sister, just five years old, and told her to roast it over the fire and present it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing her groans he resolved that flesh from his thigh could feed her; he sharpened a kitchen knife, cut four inches from his right thigh, and gave the piece to his five-year-old sister to roast and serve.

sentences.zh: 母疾良已，孟卿歸，察斅孚足微跛，得其狀，與母持以哭。

translations.literal: His mother's illness soon recovered; when Mengqing returned he noticed Xiaofu's leg was slightly lame, learned what had happened, and he and the mother held the child and wept.
translations.idiomatic: His mother soon recovered; when Mengqing returned he noticed Xiaofu limping slightly, learned what had happened, and held him with his mother, weeping.

sentences.zh: 斅孚曰：「毋然，兒固無所苦也。

translations.literal: Xiaofu said, "Do not, I truly feel no pain.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofu said, "Please don't — I feel no pain at all.

sentences.zh: 」鄉人皆嗟異稱孝童。

translations.literal: " Villagers all sighed in wonder and called him the Filial Child.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers marveled and called him the Filial Child.

sentences.zh: 長為諸生，學政溫忠翰疏聞，尋除華容訓導。

translations.literal: When grown he became a licentiate; Educational Commissioner Wen Zhonghan memorialized the throne; soon he was appointed instructor at Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he became a licentiate; Educational Commissioner Wen Zhonghan reported his story to the throne, and he was soon appointed instructor at Huarong.

sentences.zh: 孟卿亦嘗刲股愈父病，然斅孚割股時，初不知父有是事也。

translations.literal: Mengqing had also once cut flesh from his thigh to cure his father's illness, but when Xiaofu cut his flesh he had not known his father had done such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqing too had once cut his thigh to cure his own father's illness — but when Xiaofu acted he did not yet know his father had done the same.

sentences.zh: 王子明，甘肅通渭人。

translations.literal: Wang Ziming was a native of Tongwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziming came from Tongwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 事母孝。

translations.literal: Filial in serving his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted and filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 出為客，蔬果新出，必遙獻乃食。

translations.literal: Going away as a guest, whenever fruits and vegetables newly appeared, he would always send them from afar as offerings before eating.
translations.idiomatic: While working away from home, he never tasted newly ripened fruit or vegetables until he had first sent them to his mother.

sentences.zh: 嘗赴試，母聞桃香久不散，女曰：「此必吾兄所獻。

translations.literal: Once going to take the examinations, his mother smelled peach fragrance that long did not disperse; the daughter said, "This must be what my elder brother sent."
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he went off to sit for the examinations; at home his mother noticed the scent of peaches lingering unusually long, and his sister said, "That must be from our brother's offering."

sentences.zh: 」記其日，歸驗之，果然。

translations.literal: Recording that day, when he returned they verified it, and indeed it was so.
translations.idiomatic: She noted the date; when he came home they checked, and it matched exactly.

sentences.zh: 馮星明，甘肅秦安人。

translations.literal: Feng Xingming was a native of Qin'an in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingming came from Qin'an in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 為營卒，戍龍山。

translations.literal: He served as a camp soldier garrisoned at Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was a garrison soldier posted at Longshan.

sentences.zh: 食新韭，置諸案，叩首。

translations.literal: Eating fresh chives, he placed them on the table and kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: When he ate fresh chives, he set them on the table and kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 同伍問之，曰：「以獻母。

translations.literal: His fellows in the tent asked why; he said, "To offer them to my mother."
translations.idiomatic: His barracks mates asked why; he said, "To offer them to my mother."

sentences.zh: 」咸以為迂。

translations.literal: They all regarded this as pedantic.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone thought him impractical.

sentences.zh: 或歸候其母，母曰：「他日吾假寐，夢兒以韭食我，覺，猶有餘香。

translations.literal: Someone who returned home called on his mother; the mother said, "The other day I dozed off and dreamed my son fed me chives; when I woke, there was still lingering fragrance."
translations.idiomatic: Someone who went home visited his mother; she said, "The other day I dozed off and dreamed my son fed me chives—when I woke, the scent still lingered."

sentences.zh: 」叩其日，星明獻韭時也。

translations.literal: They asked the date—it was exactly when Xingming had offered the chives.
translations.idiomatic: They asked the date: it was exactly when Xingming had offered the chives.

sentences.zh: 張元翰，直隸南皮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanhan was a native of Nanpi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanhan came from Nanpi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年舉人，除獲鹿教諭，遷知縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Guangxu reign he passed the provincial examinations; he was appointed instructor at Huolu and later promoted to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examinations, was appointed instructor at Huolu, and later rose to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 方謁京師，父嗣陶時為萬全教諭，卒官。

translations.literal: While visiting the capital to pay respects, his father Sitao was then instructor at Wanquan and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: While he was in the capital paying his respects, his father Sitao, then instructor at Wanquan, died in office.

sentences.zh: 元翰奔赴慟哭，幾不能勝。

translations.literal: Yuanhan rushed there and wept until he nearly collapsed from grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan rushed to the scene and wept until he nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 居喪三年，悉用古禮。

translations.literal: He observed the three-year mourning period, employing the full ancient rites throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He observed three years of mourning and followed the full ancient rites throughout.

sentences.zh: 喪終，以知縣待缺河南，奉母赴官，攝澠池、寧陵諸縣。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, awaiting a county appointment in Henan, he brought his mother to take up office and served as acting magistrate at Mianchi, Ningling, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he awaited a county appointment in Henan, brought his mother to take up office, and served as acting magistrate at Mianchi, Ningling, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 方有事於考城，而母遽卒，元翰以父母卒皆不克視終事，大痛。

translations.literal: While occupied with affairs at Kaocheng, his mother suddenly died; Yuanhan, grieved that for both parents he had been unable to attend them at the end, was stricken with deep pain.
translations.idiomatic: While he was occupied with affairs at Kaocheng, his mother suddenly died; Yuanhan, anguished that he had been unable to see either parent through to the end, was overwhelmed with grief.

sentences.zh: 將歸葬，自為文祭告，憑棺一慟而絕。

translations.literal: About to return home for burial, he composed a text to announce the burial to his parents, leaned upon the coffin in a single burst of grief, and expired.
translations.idiomatic: About to return home for burial, he wrote a memorial text to announce it to his parents, leaned on the coffin in one convulsive burst of grief, and died.

sentences.zh: 俞鴻慶，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Yu Hongqing was a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hongqing came from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 光緒十八年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 事父母篤孝。

translations.literal: He was deeply filial in serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply devoted and filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 官京師，歲必乞假歸省。

translations.literal: While serving in the capital, every year he would request leave to return home and visit them.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the capital, he requested leave every year to return home and visit them.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，母歾，鴻慶方自西安還京師，聞喪奔還，哀慟若不欲生。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year his mother died; Hongqing had just returned from Xi'an to the capital, and on hearing of the bereavement he rushed back, grieving as though he wished not to live.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year his mother died; Hongqing had just returned from Xi'an to the capital, and on hearing the news he rushed home, grieving as though he no longer wished to live.

sentences.zh: 父年已八十，衰病，鴻慶跬步不去側，婉容愉色，依慕如少時。

translations.literal: His father was already eighty, enfeebled and ill; Hongqing never left his side a step, wearing a gentle expression and cheerful countenance, clinging to him as in childhood.
translations.idiomatic: His father was already eighty, frail and ill; Hongqing never left his side, wearing a gentle expression and cheerful face, clinging to him as in childhood.

sentences.zh: 冬夜必數起省視，或竟夕不眠。

translations.literal: On winter nights he invariably rose several times to look in on him, sometimes going the whole night without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: On winter nights he invariably rose several times to look in on him, sometimes staying awake the whole night.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，父歾，鴻慶慟甚，以毀卒，距父勿方匝月。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year his father died; Hongqing grieved intensely and died from the strain of mourning, not yet a full month after his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year his father died; Hongqing grieved intensely and died from the strain of mourning, less than a full month after his father.

sentences.zh: 姜瑢，雲南習峨人。

translations.literal: Jiang Rong was a native of Xie'e in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Rong came from Xie'e in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 父文柄，嘗遠遊，瑢裹糧行求，得以歸。

translations.literal: His father Wenbing once traveled far away; Rong packed provisions and went searching until he found him and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenbing once traveled far away; Rong packed provisions, went searching for him, found him, and brought him home.

sentences.zh: 貧，析薪治圃以養。

translations.literal: Poor, he split firewood and tended a garden to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as he was, he split firewood and tended a garden to support his father.

sentences.zh: 父嗜飲，日必具酒，家益貧，父為罷飲。

translations.literal: His father loved drink and required wine every day; the household grew poorer, and the father stopped drinking on their account.
translations.idiomatic: His father loved wine and required it every day; the household grew poorer, and the father gave up drinking on their account.

sentences.zh: 命子跪而請，翌日偕樵於山，買酒歸，共勸酣飲，日以為常。

translations.literal: Rong ordered his son to kneel and plead; the next day he went up the mountain with him for firewood, bought wine on the way home, and together they urged him to drink heartily—this became a daily habit.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had his son kneel and plead with him; the next day he went up the mountain with his father to gather firewood, bought wine on the way home, and together they urged him to drink freely—this became their daily custom.

sentences.zh: 父歾，輒提父嘗飲壺沽酒，哭於墓，人稱其圃為「孝子圃」。

translations.literal: After his father died, he would take his father's old wine flask to buy wine and weep at the grave; people called his garden the "Filial Son's Garden."
translations.idiomatic: After his father died, he would take his father's old wine flask to buy wine and weep at the grave; people called his garden the "Filial Son's Garden."

sentences.zh: 湯淵，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Tang Yuan was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yuan came from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 八歲喪父。

translations.literal: At eight he lost his father.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of eight.

sentences.zh: 母茅紡織不稍休，淵見輒淚下。

translations.literal: His mother Mao spun and wove without resting; Yuan wept whenever he saw her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Mao spun and wove without pause; Yuan wept whenever he saw her.

sentences.zh: 少長，為負販，勸母暫休，母曰：「休，不且餒死耶？

translations.literal: When he grew up he worked as a peddler and urged his mother to rest briefly; she said, "If I rest, won't we starve to death?"
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he worked as a peddler and urged his mother to rest; she said, "If I rest, won't we starve?"

sentences.zh: 」淵大慟。

translations.literal: Yuan wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 客至，母擎茗椀呼淵持以出，淵跪而受，自責貧不能具僕婢也。

translations.literal: When guests arrived, his mother would call Yuan with a tea tray to serve them; Yuan knelt to receive it, blaming himself for being too poor to keep servants.
translations.idiomatic: When guests arrived, his mother would call Yuan with a tea tray to serve them; Yuan knelt to receive it, reproaching himself for being too poor to keep servants.

sentences.zh: 娶，生子而婦亡，或勸再娶，曰：「吾已有子，何忍分養母力以養婦？

translations.literal: He married and had a son, then his wife died; some urged him to remarry, but he said, "I already have a son—how could I bear to divert my mother's strength from supporting her to supporting a wife?"
translations.idiomatic: He married and had a son, then his wife died; some urged him to remarry, but he said, "I already have a son—how could I bear to divert my mother's strength from caring for her to caring for a wife?"

sentences.zh: 」竟以鰥終。

translations.literal: He remained a widower to the end.
translations.idiomatic: He remained a widower for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀號動行路。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his wailing moved everyone on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his wailing moved everyone who passed on the road.

sentences.zh: 其後家稍裕，方冬，有被而無褥，曰：「吾母昔無此也。

translations.literal: Later when the household grew somewhat better off, in winter he had a quilt but no mattress, and said, "My mother never had this in her day."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the household grew somewhat better off, in winter he had a quilt but no mattress, and said, "My mother never had this in her day."

sentences.zh: 」將卒，命市棺視殯母之費。

translations.literal: Approaching death, he ordered that a coffin be purchased costing no more than had been spent on his mother's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached, he ordered that his coffin cost no more than had been spent on his mother's funeral.

sentences.zh: 魏興，直隸新城人。

translations.literal: Wei Xing was a native of Xincheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xing came from Xincheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 早喪父，興與弟繼宗皆入伍。

translations.literal: Having lost his father early, both Xing and his younger brother Jizong enlisted as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his father early, both Xing and his younger brother Jizong enlisted as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 繼宗戰死，興以母老，出伍為樵以養。

translations.literal: Jizong died in battle; Xing, because his mother was old, left the ranks to chop firewood and support her.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong died in battle; Xing, because his mother was old, left military service to chop firewood and support her.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，米貴，興以米奉母，而自食糟糠，恆不飽。

translations.literal: In a famine year when rice was costly, Xing gave rice to his mother while he himself ate chaff and husks, constantly going hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year when rice was costly, Xing gave rice to his mother while he himself ate chaff and husks, always going hungry.

sentences.zh: 興亦老，樵不足，毀屋，伐屋後樹以鬻。

translations.literal: When Xing also grew old and firewood hauling was insufficient, he tore down the house and sold the trees behind it for lumber.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing also grew old and firewood earnings were insufficient, he tore down the house and sold the trees behind it.

sentences.zh: 安康諸生張鵬翼聞其事，過興，見興侍母左右扶持如童子，因問其鄰魏叟：「與其母日何食？

translations.literal: Zhang Pengyi, a licentiate of Ankang, hearing of this, passed by and saw Xing supporting his mother at his side like a child, and asked the neighbor Old Wei: "What do they eat each day?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pengyi, a licentiate of Ankang, hearing of this, passed by and saw Xing supporting his mother at his side like a child; he asked the neighbor Old Wei, "What do they eat each day?"

sentences.zh: 」鄰曰：「興敢包穀，母食麥。

translations.literal: The neighbor said, "Xing dares only eat coarse millet; his mother eats wheat."
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor said, "Xing dares only eat coarse grain; his mother eats wheat."

sentences.zh: 」鵬翼大嗟異，以其事白知府，月予以粟，興母子始得飽。

translations.literal: Pengyi marveled greatly, reported the matter to the prefect, who granted them monthly grain rations; only then could mother and son eat their fill.
translations.idiomatic: Pengyi marveled greatly, reported the matter to the prefect, who granted them monthly grain; only then could mother and son eat their fill.

sentences.zh: 戴兆笨，安徽旌德人。

translations.literal: Dai Zhaoben was a native of Jingde in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhaoben came from Jingde in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少從父業縫紉，十三喪母，盡禮，事後母如母。

translations.literal: From youth he followed his father's trade of needlework; at thirteen his mother died—he performed the full rites and treated his stepmother as his own mother.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he followed his father's trade of needlework; at thirteen his mother died—he performed the full rites and treated his stepmother as his own mother.

sentences.zh: 父病噎，亦減飲食，百方療父，不得，則刲肱糜以進，終不愈。

translations.literal: When his father suffered from a choking illness, he also reduced his food and drink; he tried every means to cure his father, and when none availed he cut flesh from his arm, ground it to a paste, and fed it to him, but still he did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: When his father suffered from a choking illness, he also reduced his food and drink; he tried every remedy, and when none availed he cut flesh from his arm, ground it to a paste, and fed it to him—but still his father did not recover.

sentences.zh: 慟甚，廬墓側，朝夕稽顙。

translations.literal: Grief-stricken, he built a hut beside the tomb and morning and evening prostrated himself in kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: Grief-stricken, he built a hut beside the tomb and morning and evening kowtowed in prostration.

sentences.zh: 時歸省後母，呼妻出，戒以善侍養，不入其室。

translations.literal: Sometimes he returned home to visit his stepmother, calling his wife outside to instruct her to serve her well, and did not enter her chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he returned home to visit his stepmother, called his wife outside to instruct her to serve her well, and did not enter her chamber.

sentences.zh: 潘周岱，安徽涇縣人。

translations.literal: Pan Zhoudai was a native of Jing County in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhoudai came from Jing County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 為竹工，與父同傭，必躬其勞而遺父易且逸者。

translations.literal: A bamboo craftsman, he worked with his father as hired laborers; he always kept the hard tasks for himself and gave his father the easier ones.
translations.idiomatic: A bamboo craftsman, he worked with his father as hired laborers; he always kept the hard tasks for himself and gave his father the lighter ones.

sentences.zh: 父創足，負以往返。

translations.literal: When his father's feet were injured, he carried him back and forth on his back.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's feet were injured, he carried him back and forth on his back.

sentences.zh: 老廢，周岱獨應傭，得酒肉時蔬懷歸，燂以進。

translations.literal: When his father grew old and disabled, Zhoudai alone took on hired work; whenever he got wine, meat, or fresh vegetables he carried them home, blanched them, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: When his father grew old and disabled, Zhoudai alone took on hired work; whenever he got wine, meat, or fresh vegetables he carried them home, blanched them, and presented them to his father.

sentences.zh: 家食，必父母食乃食。

translations.literal: At meals at home, he always waited until his parents had eaten before he would eat.
translations.idiomatic: At home he always waited until his parents had eaten before he would eat.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奉父母必豐，次以食弟，躬與妻子飽糠覈。

translations.literal: In famine years he gave his parents plentiful portions, then his younger brother, while he and his wife and children themselves ate chaff and husks until full.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he gave his parents generous portions, then his younger brother, while he and his wife and children ate chaff and husks themselves.

sentences.zh: 父母疾，左右侍養無須臾去側。

translations.literal: When his parents fell ill, he attended them at their side without leaving for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents fell ill, he attended them at their side without leaving for a moment.

sentences.zh: 母家山下泉洌，母病篤，夜半思得泉以飲，周岱挈瓶往，行四十餘裡，鄉晨以泉至。

translations.literal: At the foot of the mountain behind their home was a spring of pure water; when his mother was critically ill and at midnight craved this water to drink, Zhoudai took a jar and went—over forty li—and returned at dawn with the spring water.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of the mountain behind their home was a spring of pure water; when his mother was critically ill and at midnight craved this water, Zhoudai took a jar and walked more than forty li, returning at dawn with the spring water.

sentences.zh: 居喪，旦暮悲號，先後廬墓三年。

translations.literal: During mourning he wailed morning and evening and built mourning huts beside the tombs in succession for three years.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he wailed morning and evening and built mourning huts beside the tombs for three years in succession.

sentences.zh: 喪既終，夕必詣墓爇香燃燈，如是終其身。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, each evening he still went to the graves to burn incense and light lamps, and did so for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, each evening he still went to the graves to burn incense and light lamps, and did so for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 妻吳亦孝，無違命。

translations.literal: His wife Wu was also filial and never disobeyed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Wu was also filial and never disobeyed his commands.

sentences.zh: 張淮，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Huai was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huai came from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 貧，粗識字，為人收田租。

translations.literal: Poor and barely literate, he collected land rents for others.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and barely literate, he collected land rents for others.

sentences.zh: 父有心疾，思食羊，非特殺則不食，淮買羊殺以食父。

translations.literal: His father had a heart ailment and craved mutton—but would not eat it unless specially slaughtered; Huai bought a sheep, slaughtered it, and fed his father.
translations.idiomatic: His father had a heart ailment and craved mutton—but would eat it only if freshly slaughtered; Huai bought a sheep, slaughtered it, and fed his father.

sentences.zh: 思出遊，則賃肩輿侍以出，窮日乃還。

translations.literal: When he wished to go out, Huai hired a sedan chair and accompanied him all day until evening before returning.
translations.idiomatic: When his father wished to go out, Huai hired a sedan chair and accompanied him from morning until evening before returning.

sentences.zh: 父疾數年，凡所思，百方致之，不稍怠。

translations.literal: His father's illness lasted several years; whatever he desired, Huai obtained it by every means, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: His father's illness lasted several years; whatever he desired, Huai obtained it by every means, never slackening.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，刲肱進，卒不治。

translations.literal: When the illness became critical, he cut flesh from his arm and fed it to him, but still he could not be cured.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness became critical, he cut flesh from his arm and fed it to him, but still his father could not be cured.

sentences.zh: 同時張廷標，為衣工。

translations.literal: At the same time Zhang Tingbiao was a clothes-maker.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Zhang Tingbiao was a clothes-maker.

sentences.zh: 奉母，常效市中兒嬉戲以娛母。

translations.literal: Supporting his mother, he often mimicked children playing in the marketplace to amuse her.
translations.idiomatic: Supporting his mother, he often mimicked children playing in the marketplace to amuse her.

sentences.zh: 一日鄰家火，負母出，遷祀先之具，而不及他器用。

translations.literal: One day a neighbor's house caught fire; he carried his mother out and moved the ancestors' ritual vessels, but had no time for other possessions.
translations.idiomatic: One day a neighbor's house caught fire; he carried his mother out and moved the ancestors' ritual vessels, but had no time for other possessions.

sentences.zh: 節所入為弟娶婦，而終身不自娶。

translations.literal: He set aside from his earnings to find a wife for his younger brother, and never married himself.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside from his earnings to find a wife for his younger brother, and never married himself.

sentences.zh: 縣人與淮稱「二孝子」，道光初年事也。

translations.literal: People in the county called Huai and him the "Two Filial Sons"—this was in the early Daoguang period.
translations.idiomatic: People in the county called Huai and him the "Two Filial Sons"—this occurred in the early Daoguang period.

sentences.zh: 胡其愛，江南桐城人。

translations.literal: Hu Qiai was a native of Tongcheng south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qiai came from Tongcheng in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 為人傭而養母。

translations.literal: He worked as a hired laborer to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He worked as a hired laborer to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 母病疲癃，其愛日夕在左右，視臥起飲食。

translations.literal: His mother was ill and paralyzed; Qiai stayed constantly at her side day and night, watching over her sleeping, rising, eating, and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was ill and bedridden with paralysis; Qiai stayed constantly at her side day and night, watching over her sleeping, rising, eating, and drinking.

sentences.zh: 出就傭，具晨餐，度午不能歸，出勺米付鄰媼，囑代爨，必拜。

translations.literal: Going out for hired work, he prepared her morning meal; estimating he could not return by midday, he brought out a spoonful of rice for a neighbor woman, entrusting her to cook it—always with a bow.
translations.idiomatic: Going out for hired work, he prepared her morning meal; estimating he could not return by midday, he brought out a spoonful of rice for a neighbor woman and entrusted her to cook it—always with a bow.

sentences.zh: 鄰媼止之，行數里外，复遙拜。

translations.literal: The neighbor woman would stop him, but he had gone several li and still turned to bow from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor woman would stop him, but even after he had gone several li he still turned to bow from afar.

sentences.zh: 夜必歸，為母滌中裙廁牏。

translations.literal: Each night he returned to wash her undergarments and toilet for her.
translations.idiomatic: Each night he returned to wash her undergarments and clean her toilet for her.

sentences.zh: 在傭家得肉食，即請歸遺母。

translations.literal: When he received meat at his employer's house, he immediately asked leave to bring it home as a gift for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he received meat at his employer's house, he immediately asked leave to bring it home for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母出觀優，負以往，夜則負以還。

translations.literal: When his mother went out to watch opera performances, he carried her there; at night he carried her back.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother went out to watch opera performances, he carried her there; at night he carried her back.

sentences.zh: 欲往戚黨家，亦如之。

translations.literal: When she wished to visit relatives, he did the same.
translations.idiomatic: When she wished to visit relatives, he did the same.

sentences.zh: 母歿，負土為墳，居悒悒而卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he carried earth to build her grave and died dejected and grieving.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he carried earth to build her grave and died dejected and grieving.

sentences.zh: 方其明，亦桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Qiming was also from Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qiming was also from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 亦為傭而養母，母亦病疲癃。

translations.literal: He too worked as a hired laborer to support his mother; his mother was also ill and bedridden with paralysis.
translations.idiomatic: He too worked as a hired laborer to support his mother; his mother was also ill and bedridden with paralysis.

sentences.zh: 其明慮出傭母飢渴，乃棄傭為丐，負母以出，得食必先母。

translations.literal: Qiming, fearing that while away at hired work his mother might hunger or thirst, gave up hired labor and became a beggar, carrying his mother when he went out; whenever he got food he always gave it to his mother first.
translations.idiomatic: Qiming, fearing that while away at hired work his mother might hunger or thirst, gave up hired labor and became a beggar, carrying his mother when he went out; whenever he got food he always gave it to his mother first.

sentences.zh: 母卒，乃為圃，時荷鋤而泣曰：「昔為乞，苦飢寒，不離母側；

translations.literal: After his mother died, he worked a vegetable garden; sometimes leaning on his hoe he would weep and say, "In the past as a beggar, though suffering hunger and cold, I never left my mother's side;
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, he worked a vegetable garden; sometimes leaning on his hoe he would weep and say, "In the past as a beggar, though suffering hunger and cold, I never left my mother's side;

sentences.zh: 今稍足衣食，思母不可得矣！

translations.literal: Now I have somewhat enough in clothing and food—yet I think of my mother and cannot have her anymore!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I have somewhat enough in clothing and food—yet I think of my mother and cannot have her anymore!"

sentences.zh: 鄧成珠，福建泰宁人。

translations.literal: Deng Chengzhu was a native of Taining in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chengzhu came from Taining in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 亦為傭而養母。

translations.literal: He too worked as a hired laborer to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He too worked as a hired laborer to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 傭所距家遠，日乞米一合，昧旦送母所，還執傭。

translations.literal: The place where he worked was far from home; each day he begged a he of rice, set out before dawn to deliver it to his mother, then returned to his hired work.
translations.idiomatic: The place where he worked was far from home; each day he begged a he of rice, set out before dawn to deliver it to his mother, then returned to his hired work.

sentences.zh: 母盲不能炊，乃負母依主家傍舍，朝夕為具食。

translations.literal: His mother was blind and unable to cook; so he carried his mother to lodge in a side shed beside his master's house, preparing food morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was blind and unable to cook; so he carried his mother to lodge in a side shed beside his master's house, preparing food morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 主或以為言，成珠曰：「成珠自減餐奉母，不敢重累主人也。

translations.literal: The master sometimes remarked on this; Chengzhu said, "Chengzhu reduces his own meals to support his mother—I dare not burden the master further."
translations.idiomatic: The master sometimes remarked on this; Chengzhu said, "Chengzhu reduces his own meals to support his mother—I dare not burden the master further."

sentences.zh: 」居五年，母卒，葬畢，辭主人，不知所之。

translations.literal: " After five years his mother died; when the burial was complete, he took leave of his master and went away—no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: " After five years his mother died; when the burial was complete, he took leave of his master and departed—no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 張三愛，江南歙縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang San'ai was a native of She County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang San'ai came from She County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 為人役。

translations.literal: He worked in service to others.
translations.idiomatic: He worked in service to others.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，母病，不能具藥物。

translations.literal: Filial in serving his mother; when his mother fell ill he could not afford medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his mother; when she fell ill he could not afford medicine.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「汝欲愈母病，盍刲肝？

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "If you wish to cure your mother's illness, why not cut out your liver?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "If you want to cure your mother's illness, why not cut out your liver?"

sentences.zh: 」三愛禱於叢祠，破腹，肝墮出，以右手劙肝，得指許，左手納於腹，束以白麻。

translations.literal: San'ai prayed at a roadside shrine, opened his belly, and when his liver fell out he sliced off a piece about the size of a finger with his right hand, pushed it back into his belly with his left, and bound it with white hemp.
translations.idiomatic: San'ai prayed at a roadside shrine, opened his belly, and when his liver fell out he sliced off a piece about the size of a finger with his right hand, pushed it back in with his left, and bound the wound with white hemp.

sentences.zh: 歸以肝和羹飲母，母良愈，三愛創亦合。

translations.literal: Returning home he made a soup with the liver and fed it to his mother; she recovered fully, and San'ai's wound also closed.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home he made a soup with the liver and fed it to his mother; she recovered fully, and San'ai's wound closed as well.

sentences.zh: 三愛所事主，故嘗為知縣，貧，逋賦，三愛輒代承，被笞，不少懟。

translations.literal: The master San'ai served had formerly been a county magistrate; poor, he had fallen behind in taxes—San'ai always assumed the debt and was flogged, never protesting.
translations.idiomatic: The master San'ai served had once been a county magistrate; poor and in arrears on taxes, San'ai always assumed the debt and was flogged without protest.

sentences.zh: 主病且死，命三愛去，三愛勿聽，事主之子如事主。

translations.literal: When the master was ill and near death he ordered San'ai to leave; San'ai would not listen and served the master's son as he had served the master.
translations.idiomatic: When the master was ill and near death he ordered San'ai to leave; San'ai refused and served the master's son as he had served the master.

sentences.zh: 楊夢益，陝西郃陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Mengyi was a native of Heyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mengyi came from Heyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 賣菜傭也，事母孝，妻賈力紡織以佐養。

translations.literal: A vegetable vendor and hired laborer, filial toward his mother; his wife toiled at spinning and weaving to help support them.
translations.idiomatic: A vegetable vendor and hired laborer, he was filial toward his mother; his wife toiled at spinning and weaving to help support them.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，歲饑，夢益與妻食糠籺，盛米於囊，置其中，熟以奉母。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period, during a famine year, Mengyi and his wife ate bran cakes while placing rice in a bag and cooking it to serve their mother.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign, in a famine year, Mengyi and his wife ate bran cakes while placing rice in a bag and cooking it to serve their mother.

sentences.zh: 米盡，將鬻子，族人感而周之，乃止。

translations.literal: When the rice ran out they were about to sell their son; the clan, moved, gave them relief and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the rice ran out they were about to sell their son; the clan, moved, gave them relief and they abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 閻天倫，甘肅隴​​西人。

translations.literal: Yan Tianlun was a native of Longxi in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tianlun came from Longxi in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 貧，父居僧寺，天倫與妻楊，雞鳴起磨面，及明入市，求父所嗜往饋，午若晡皆然，夜則從父寢。

translations.literal: Poor, with his father living in a Buddhist temple, Tianlun and his wife Yang rose at cockcrow to grind flour; at daylight they entered the market, sought what his father loved, and brought it to feed him—at midday and in the evening alike; at night he slept beside his father.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, with his father living in a Buddhist temple, Tianlun and his wife Yang rose at cockcrow to grind flour; at daylight they entered the market, sought what his father loved, and brought it to him—at midday and in the evening alike; at night he slept beside his father.

sentences.zh: 父失明，天倫為茹素，年餘，目復明。

translations.literal: When his father lost his sight, Tianlun ate vegetarian for more than a year, and his father's eyes regained their sight.
translations.idiomatic: When his father lost his sight, Tianlun ate vegetarian for more than a year, and his father's eyes regained their sight.

sentences.zh: 天倫先父卒，楊賣漿為養，如天倫在時。

translations.literal: Tianlun died before his father; Yang sold soy milk to support him, just as when Tianlun was alive.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlun died before his father; Yang sold soy milk to support him, just as when Tianlun had been alive.

sentences.zh: 翁卒，力營葬，忌日必祭，終其身。

translations.literal: When the old father died she exerted herself to arrange burial and on the anniversary of death always made offerings—throughout her life.
translations.idiomatic: When the old father died she exerted herself to arrange burial and on each anniversary of his death made offerings—for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 夏士友，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: Xia Shiyou was a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shiyou came from Jiangxia in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，傭力以養，不足，則減己食食母。

translations.literal: Filial toward his mother, he worked for wages to support her; when that was insufficient he reduced his own food to feed her.
translations.idiomatic: Filial toward his mother, he worked for wages to support her; when that was insufficient he reduced his own food to feed her.

sentences.zh: 鄰或邀食，必先為母具食，然後往。

translations.literal: When neighbors invited him to eat he always prepared food for his mother first, then went.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors invited him to eat he always prepared food for his mother first, then went.

sentences.zh: 寒，語母勿早起，自執炊置食床前，又丁寧囑母善自護，乃出，如是以為常。

translations.literal: In cold weather he told his mother not to rise early; he himself cooked and placed food by her bed, earnestly urging her to take good care of herself, then went out—this was his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: In cold weather he told his mother not to rise early; he himself cooked and placed food by her bed, earnestly urging her to take good care of herself, then went out—this was his constant practice.

sentences.zh: 年四十未娶，或愍之，助其娶婦。

translations.literal: At forty he had not yet married; some pitying him helped him take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he had not yet married; some who pitied him helped him take a wife.

sentences.zh: 居半載，士友自外歸，婦與姑詬於室，流涕責婦，即日出之。

translations.literal: After half a year Shiyou returned from outside and found his wife quarreling with his mother in the room; weeping, he scolded his wife and sent her away that same day.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year Shiyou returned from outside and found his wife quarreling with his mother in the room; weeping, he scolded his wife and sent her away that same day.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「出婦，如無後何？

translations.literal: Some said, "If you send away your wife, what of having no posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "If you send away your wife, what of having no posterity?"

sentences.zh: 」士友曰：「有婦，欲其孝；

translations.literal: Shiyou said, "Having a wife, one wants her to be filial;
translations.idiomatic: Shiyou said, "Having a wife, one wants her to be filial;

sentences.zh: 有子孫，亦欲其孝。

translations.literal: Having descendants, one also wants them to be filial.
translations.idiomatic: Having descendants, one also wants them to be filial.

sentences.zh: 苟不孝，安用婦？

translations.literal: If there is no filial piety, what use is a wife?
translations.idiomatic: If there is no filial piety, what use is a wife?

sentences.zh: 安用子孫？

translations.literal: What use are descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: What use are descendants?"

sentences.zh: 」年餘，士友疾卒，母哭之慟，鄰有張某感士友孝而不得終事母，月供薪米，終其身。

translations.literal: After more than a year Shiyou died suddenly of illness; his mother wept bitterly. A neighbor surnamed Zhang, moved that Shiyou's filial piety had not let him finish serving his mother, supplied firewood and rice monthly for the rest of her life.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year Shiyou died suddenly of illness; his mother wept bitterly. A neighbor surnamed Zhang, moved that Shiyou's filial devotion had not let him finish serving his mother, supplied firewood and rice monthly for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 白長久，甘肅平番人。

translations.literal: Bai Changjiu was a native of Pingfan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Changjiu came from Pingfan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，貧，負販奉母，具甘旨。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he peddled on his back to support his mother with delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he peddled on his back to support his mother with delicacies.

sentences.zh: 母或不怡，以首抵母，引手披其頸，俟解乃止。

translations.literal: When his mother was displeased, he pressed his head against her and gently stroked her neck with his hand, waiting until she was soothed before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was displeased, he pressed his head against her and gently stroked her neck, waiting until she was soothed before stopping.

sentences.zh: 里社演劇，負母往觀，侍側說劇中事。

translations.literal: When the village temple put on plays he carried his mother to watch, standing at her side and explaining the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the village temple put on plays he carried his mother to watch, standing at her side and explaining the plot.

sentences.zh: 母年八十，長久亦六十，未嘗稍懈。

translations.literal: When his mother was eighty, Changjiu was also sixty, and he never slackened in the least.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was eighty, Changjiu was also sixty, and he never slackened in the least.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，青海辦事大臣豫師餽以金，不受。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu period, Yushi, the Qing commissioner in Qinghai, sent him gold, which he refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu period, Yushi, the Qing commissioner in Qinghai, sent him gold, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 母卒，朝夕詣墓，饋食三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died he morning and evening visited her tomb and brought food offerings for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he visited her tomb morning and evening and brought food offerings for three years.

sentences.zh: 郭味兒，甘肅禮縣人。

translations.literal: Guo Weier was a native of Li County in Gansu.
