translations.idiomatic: Guo Weier came from Li County in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 賣漿，出必拜母，歸亦然。

translations.literal: He sold soy milk; going out he always bowed to his mother, and returning was the same.
translations.idiomatic: He sold soy milk; going out he always bowed to his mother, and returning was the same.

sentences.zh: 母嚴，稍不當意即恚，味兒為孺子狀悅母。

translations.literal: His mother was strict; the slightest dissatisfaction brought her anger—Weier would act like a child to please her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was strict; the slightest dissatisfaction brought her anger—Weier would act like a child to please her.

sentences.zh: 母苦脛痛，或言瘞枯骨，母當愈，黎明輒攜長鑱徘徊丘隴間，寒暑不間。

translations.literal: When his mother suffered from leg pain, someone said burying exposed bones would cure her; at dawn he always took a long spade and wandered among the hills and mounds, without interruption in heat or cold.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother suffered from leg pain, someone said burying exposed bones would cure her; at dawn he always took a long spade and wandered among the hills and mounds, without interruption in heat or cold.

sentences.zh: 母卒，飲不入口，五日毀卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died he would not take food or drink and died from grief in five days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he would not take food or drink and died from grief within five days.

sentences.zh: 聶宏，陝西鄠縣人。

translations.literal: Nie Hong was a native of Hu County in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Hong came from Hu County in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 賣酒，事親孝，得錢易甘脆奉親。

translations.literal: He sold wine, filial in serving his parents; with money earned he bought delicacies for them.
translations.idiomatic: He sold wine and was filial in serving his parents; with money earned he bought delicacies for them.

sentences.zh: 母卒，臥父榻側，時省視。

translations.literal: When his mother died he slept beside his father's couch and checked on him frequently.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he slept beside his father's couch and checked on him frequently.

sentences.zh: 畜犬，得餅銜飼母，人以為孝感。

translations.literal: He kept a dog; when it got a cake it carried it in its mouth to feed his mother—people took this as a sign of filial response from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a dog; when it got a cake it carried it in its mouth to feed his mother—people took this as a sign of filial response from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 董阿虎，江南山陽人。

translations.literal: Dong Ahu was a native of Shanyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ahu came from Shanyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少喪父，為人擔水，得值養母。

translations.literal: He lost his father young and carried water for others, using the wages to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father young and carried water for others, using the wages to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 稍有餘，必具甘旨。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a little surplus he always provided delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had a little surplus he always provided delicacies.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，構茅屋奉母。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years he built a thatched hut to shelter his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than ten years he built a thatched hut to shelter his mother.

sentences.zh: 一日，鄰被火，阿虎負母避，還跪戶外，乞神佑。

translations.literal: One day when a neighbor's house caught fire, Ahu carried his mother to safety, then returned and knelt outside the door begging divine protection.
translations.idiomatic: One day when a neighbor's house caught fire, Ahu carried his mother to safety, then returned and knelt outside the door begging divine protection.

sentences.zh: 俄左右盡爇，獨阿虎茅屋存。

translations.literal: Soon everything around was burned, but Ahu's thatched hut alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Soon everything around was burned, but Ahu's thatched hut alone remained.

sentences.zh: 張乞人，順天永清人，失其名。

translations.literal: Zhang the Beggar was from Yongqing in Shuntian—his personal name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang the Beggar was from Yongqing in Shuntian—his personal name is lost.

sentences.zh: 父死，行乞以養母。

translations.literal: After his father died he begged alms to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died he begged alms to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 穴土為居，天大雪，知縣魏繼齊過其處，聞歌聲出地中，怪而呼問之，曰：「今日母生日，歌以勸餐耳。

translations.literal: He dug a dwelling in the earth; on a day of heavy snow the magistrate Wei Jiqi passed by and heard singing from underground; surprised, he called out and asked—the beggar said, "Today is my mother's birthday; I sing to encourage her to eat."
translations.idiomatic: He dug a dwelling in the earth; on a day of heavy snow the magistrate Wei Jiqi passed by and heard singing from underground; surprised, he called out and asked—the beggar said, "Today is my mother's birthday; I sing to encourage her to eat."

sentences.zh: 」繼齊命車載其母子至縣，繼齊母畀其母粟及布，繼齊與銀十緡。

translations.literal: Jiqi ordered a cart to bring mother and son to the county seat; Jiqi's mother gave his mother grain and cloth, and Jiqi gave ten strings of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi ordered a cart to bring mother and son to the county seat; Jiqi's mother gave his mother grain and cloth, and Jiqi gave ten strings of silver.

sentences.zh: 乞人叩頭曰：「官母賜我母，不敢不受；

translations.literal: The beggar kowtowed and said, "The magistrate's mother bestowed on my mother—I dare not refuse;
translations.idiomatic: The beggar kowtowed and said, "The magistrate's mother bestowed on my mother—I dare not refuse;

sentences.zh: 官賜我，我不敢受。

translations.literal: What the magistrate bestowed on me—I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: What the magistrate bestowed on me—I dare not accept."

sentences.zh: 」繼齊問其故，曰：「民愚，不知此十緡官何所受之？

translations.literal: Jiqi asked why; he said, "This subject is ignorant and does not know where the magistrate obtained these ten strings of silver?
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi asked why; he said, "This subject is ignorant and does not know where the magistrate obtained these ten strings of silver?

sentences.zh: 我母年八十，我年六十​​一，為清白百姓足矣。

translations.literal: My mother is eighty, I am sixty-one—to be honest common folk is enough."
translations.idiomatic: My mother is eighty, I am sixty-one—to be honest common folk is enough."

sentences.zh: 」繼齊不復強，將為營室，乞人負其母去，不知所終。

translations.literal: Jiqi did not press further and was about to build them a house; the beggar carried his mother away and was never heard from again.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi did not press further and was about to build them a house; the beggar carried his mother away and was never heard from again.

sentences.zh: 席慕孔，廣東三水人。

translations.literal: Xi Mukong was a native of Sanshui in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Mukong came from Sanshui in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 善養母。

translations.literal: He was skilled at supporting his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at supporting his mother.

sentences.zh: 嘗娶妻生子。

translations.literal: He once married and had a son.
translations.idiomatic: He once married and had a son.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，田數畝盡鬻，妻怨其貧，求去，遂遣之。

translations.literal: In a famine year he sold all several mu of fields; his wife grumbled at their poverty and asked to leave, so he sent her away.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he sold all several mu of fields; his wife grumbled at their poverty and asked to leave, so he sent her away.

sentences.zh: 夏秋助人耕穫為傭，冬則乞食以養。

translations.literal: In spring and summer he worked as hired help in plowing and harvesting; in winter he begged food to support her.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer he worked as hired help in plowing and harvesting; in winter he begged food to support her.

sentences.zh: 得餅餌歸食母，得餘羹，啜湆，以肉歸。

translations.literal: When he got cakes he brought them home for his mother to eat; with leftover soup he drank the dregs and brought home the meat.
translations.idiomatic: When he got cakes he brought them home for his mother to eat; with leftover soup he drank the dregs and brought home the meat.

sentences.zh: 張長松，山東棲霞人。

translations.literal: Zhang Changsong was a native of Qixia in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changsong came from Qixia in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 母瞽，長松出為傭，主人與之食，輒不盡，歸遺母。

translations.literal: His mother was blind; Changsong went out as a hired laborer—when his master gave him food he never finished it, returning the remainder for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was blind; Changsong went out as a hired laborer—when his master gave him food he never finished it, returning the remainder for his mother.

sentences.zh: 無所事則乞諸鄰里，母食已，乃食其餘。

translations.literal: When he had nothing to do he begged from neighbors; after his mother had eaten he ate what remained.
translations.idiomatic: When he had nothing to do he begged from neighbors; after his mother had eaten he ate what remained.

sentences.zh: 冬大雪，長松病不能出，呼母涕泣言曰：「兒不肖，不能養吾母，乃乞食，母賴以活。

translations.literal: In winter during heavy snow Changsong was ill and could not go out; calling to his mother he wept and said, "Your son is unworthy and cannot support my mother, and so we beg for food—my mother relies on that to live.
translations.idiomatic: In winter during heavy snow Changsong was ill and could not go out; calling to his mother he wept and said, "Your son is unworthy and cannot support my mother, and so we beg for food—my mother relies on that to live.

sentences.zh: 今疾憊，母老，可若何？

translations.literal: Now I am weary with illness, my mother is old—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I am weary with illness, my mother is old—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 」遂死。

translations.literal: And thereupon he died.
translations.idiomatic: And thereupon he died.

sentences.zh: 崔長生，江南邳州人。

translations.literal: Cui Changsheng was a native of Pizhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Changsheng came from Pizhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 生而瘖，手又攣。

translations.literal: Born mute, his hands were also crippled.
translations.idiomatic: Born mute, his hands were also crippled.

sentences.zh: 為傭養父母，出入必面。

translations.literal: He worked as a hired laborer to support his parents; going out and coming in he always bowed to them.
translations.idiomatic: He worked as a hired laborer to support his parents; going out and coming in he always bowed to them.

sentences.zh: 歲大祲，乞食於市，得糟糠，上父母，自食草根木實以活。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine he begged food in the market; what chaff and husks he got he gave to his parents, eating roots and tree fruit himself to survive.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of great famine he begged food in the market; what chaff and husks he got he gave to his parents, eating roots and tree fruit himself to survive.

sentences.zh: 拾字紙，得遺金，待失者踰月不得。

translations.literal: While gathering waste paper he found lost gold; he waited for the owner over a month without anyone coming.
translations.idiomatic: While gathering waste paper he found lost gold; he waited for the owner over a month without anyone coming.

sentences.zh: 乃易母彘飼之，茁壯蕃息，為父母治送死之具。

translations.literal: So he traded for a sow and raised pigs; they flourished and multiplied, and he provided funeral goods for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: So he traded for a sow and raised pigs; they flourished and multiplied, and he provided funeral goods for his parents.

sentences.zh: 喪父母，舁葬於中野，遂去，不知所終。

translations.literal: After his parents died he carried them on a bier and buried them in the open countryside, then departed—no one knew his end.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died he carried them on a bier and buried them in the open countryside, then departed—no one knew his end.

sentences.zh: 榮孝子，河南遂平人。

translations.literal: The Filial Son Rong was from Suiping in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Son Rong came from Suiping in Henan.

sentences.zh: 幼痴聾，無名。

translations.literal: From youth he was simple-minded and deaf, without a personal name.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was simple-minded and deaf, without a personal name.

sentences.zh: 家本饒，後中落，貧甚。

translations.literal: His family had once been wealthy but later declined into extreme poverty.
translations.idiomatic: His family had once been wealthy but later declined into extreme poverty.

sentences.zh: 父卒，無所居，奉母居棲流鋪。

translations.literal: When his father died, with nowhere to live, he brought his mother to dwell in a vagrants' shelter.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, with nowhere to live, he brought his mother to dwell in a vagrants' shelter.

sentences.zh: 出乞食，擇所得供母，自食其餘。

translations.literal: Going out to beg, he chose the best of what he got to supply his mother and ate the remainder himself.
translations.idiomatic: Going out to beg, he chose the best of what he got to supply his mother and ate the remainder himself.

sentences.zh: 得少，則但供母，而自忍飢歸。

translations.literal: When he got little he provided only for his mother and returned home hungry himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he got little he provided only for his mother and returned home hungry himself.

sentences.zh: 見母必叩頭，食必跪進。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw his mother he kowtowed; when offering food he always knelt to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw his mother he kowtowed; when offering food he always knelt to present it.

sentences.zh: 母食則起而舞，食減則泣。

translations.literal: When his mother ate he rose and danced; when she ate less he wept.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother ate he rose and danced; when she ate less he wept.

sentences.zh: 母或故減食以食子，則泣不受。

translations.literal: When his mother deliberately reduced her food to give some to her son, he wept and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother deliberately reduced her food to give some to her son, he wept and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 母七十餘卒，縣人為具斂，朝暮泣，終其身。

translations.literal: When his mother died past seventy the county people provided her funeral; morning and evening he wept—for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died past seventy the county people provided her funeral; morning and evening he wept—for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 吏以孝子旌其楣，亦不知孝子為何名也。

translations.literal: Officials erected a filial-son plaque on his door lintel, yet no one knew what the filial son's name was.
translations.idiomatic: Officials erected a filial-son plaque on his door lintel, yet no one knew what the filial son's name was.

sentences.zh: 卒亦七十餘。

translations.literal: He too died past seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He too died past seventy.

sentences.zh: 無錫二孝子，皆失其姓氏。

translations.literal: There were two filial sons in Wuxi, both surnames lost.
translations.idiomatic: There were two filial sons in Wuxi, both surnames lost.

sentences.zh: 其一瞽，磨粉為業，事母至孝，竭力供甘旨。

translations.literal: One was blind and made a living grinding flour; filial toward his mother to the utmost, exerting himself to provide delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: One was blind and made a living grinding flour; filial toward his mother to the utmost, he exerted himself to provide delicacies.

sentences.zh: 年至四十餘復明，人皆異之。

translations.literal: At past forty his sight was restored—all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty his sight was restored—all marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 其一啞，行乞得錢以養母，必具酒脯。

translations.literal: One was mute; he begged for money to support his mother and always provided wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: One was mute; he begged for money to support his mother and always provided wine and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 母卒，食必祭，祭必伏地號痛。

translations.literal: When his mother died, before every meal he made offerings, and at each offering he prostrated himself on the ground wailing in pain.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, before every meal he made offerings, and at each offering he prostrated himself on the ground wailing in pain.

sentences.zh: 既葬，哭於墓，見者皆感。

translations.literal: After burial he wept at the grave—all who saw were moved.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he wept at the grave—all who saw were moved.

sentences.zh: 啞孝子，無姓氏，或曰雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: The Mute Filial Son, surname unknown, said by some to be from Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Mute Filial Son, surname unknown, said by some to be from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 家有母，老矣，行乞以養。

translations.literal: He had a mother who was old; he begged alms to support her.
translations.idiomatic: He had a mother who was old; he begged alms to support her.

sentences.zh: 得食必奉母，母食然後食。

translations.literal: When he got food he always offered it to his mother; only after she had eaten would he eat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he got food he always offered it to his mother; only after she had eaten would he eat himself.

sentences.zh: 母或怒，嬉戲拜且舞，必母樂乃已。

translations.literal: When his mother was angry he would play games, bow, and dance—he would not stop until she was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew angry he would play games, bow, and dance—he would not stop until she was pleased.

sentences.zh: 得錢密投諸井，母卒，鄉人有欲醵錢以助斂者，與如井，數數指水中，鄉人為出錢，營殮且葬。

translations.literal: When he got money he secretly dropped it into a well; when his mother died and village people wished to collect money to help with burial, he led them to the well and repeatedly pointed at the water—the villagers produced the money and arranged encoffining and burial.
translations.idiomatic: When he got money he secretly dropped it into a well; when his mother died and villagers wished to collect money to help with burial, he led them to the well and repeatedly pointed at the water—the villagers produced the money and arranged encoffining and burial.

sentences.zh: 事畢，遠遊不知所終。

translations.literal: When the matter was complete he traveled far away—no one knew his end.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was complete he traveled far away—no one knew his end.
